```{r}
# =============================================================================
# 2. GENERAL HELPERS
# =============================================================================

clean_id <- function(x) {

  x <- str_trim(
    as.character(x)
  )

  x <- str_replace(
    x,
    "\\.0+$",
    ""
  )

  x[x == ""] <- NA_character_

  x
}


clean_text <- function(x) {

  x <- as.character(x)

  x[is.na(x)] <- ""

  x %>%
    str_replace_all(
      "[\r\n\t]+",
      " "
    ) %>%
    str_squish() %>%
    str_to_lower()
}


parse_group <- function(x) {

  x <- clean_text(x)

  case_when(

    str_detect(
      x,
      "control|(^|\\D)0\\s*ppm"
    ) ~
      "Control",

    str_detect(
      x,
      "(^|\\D)10\\s*ppm|(^|\\D)10($|\\D)"
    ) ~
      "10 ppm",

    str_detect(
      x,
      "(^|\\D)30\\s*ppm|(^|\\D)30($|\\D)"
    ) ~
      "30 ppm",

    str_detect(
      x,
      "(^|\\D)60\\s*ppm|(^|\\D)60($|\\D)"
    ) ~
      "60 ppm",

    TRUE ~
      NA_character_
  )
}


pick_column <- function(
  nms,
  patterns
) {

  for (p in patterns) {

    hit <- nms[
      str_detect(
        nms,
        regex(
          p,
          ignore_case = TRUE
        )
      )
    ]

    if (length(hit) > 0) {
      return(hit[1])
    }
  }

  NA_character_
}


find_sheet <- function(
  file,
  pattern
) {

  sheets <- excel_sheets(file)

  hit <- sheets[
    str_detect(
      sheets,
      regex(
        pattern,
        ignore_case = TRUE
      )
    )
  ]

  if (length(hit) == 0) {

    stop(
      paste(
        "Could not find sheet matching:",
        pattern
      )
    )
  }

  hit[1]
}


find_header_row <- function(
  file,
  sheet,
  required_terms,
  n_max = 50
) {

  preview <- read_excel(
    file,
    sheet = sheet,
    col_names = FALSE,
    col_types = "text",
    n_max = n_max,
    .name_repair = "minimal"
  )


  row_text <- apply(
    preview,
    1,
    function(x) {

      clean_text(
        paste(
          x,
          collapse = " "
        )
      )
    }
  )


  good <- rep(
    TRUE,
    length(row_text)
  )


  for (term in required_terms) {

    good <- good &
      str_detect(
        row_text,
        regex(
          term,
          ignore_case = TRUE
        )
      )
  }


  hit <- which(good)


  if (length(hit) == 0) {

    stop(
      paste(
        "Could not find header row in",
        sheet
      )
    )
  }


  hit[1]
}


parse_mixed_date <- function(x) {

  x <- str_trim(
    as.character(x)
  )

  x[x == ""] <- NA_character_


  numeric_x <- suppressWarnings(
    as.numeric(x)
  )


  out <- as.Date(
    rep(
      NA_real_,
      length(x)
    ),
    origin = "1970-01-01"
  )


  # Excel serial dates
  excel_date <- !is.na(numeric_x) &
    numeric_x > 20000 &
    numeric_x < 80000


  out[excel_date] <- as.Date(
    numeric_x[excel_date],
    origin = "1899-12-30"
  )


  remaining <- !excel_date &
    !is.na(x)


  formats <- c(
    "%Y-%m-%d",
    "%m/%d/%Y",
    "%m/%d/%y",
    "%m-%d-%Y",
    "%m-%d-%y"
  )


  for (fmt in formats) {

    idx <- remaining &
      is.na(out)

    if (!any(idx)) {
      break
    }

    out[idx] <- suppressWarnings(
      as.Date(
        x[idx],
        format = fmt
      )
    )
  }


  out
}


ordered_factor <- function(x) {

  x_chr <- as.character(x)

  levels_x <- unique(
    x_chr[
      !is.na(x_chr)
    ]
  )


  num <- suppressWarnings(
    as.numeric(
      levels_x
    )
  )


  if (
    length(levels_x) > 0 &&
    all(
      !is.na(num)
    )
  ) {

    levels_x <- levels_x[
      order(num)
    ]

  } else {

    levels_x <- sort(
      levels_x
    )
  }


  factor(
    x_chr,
    levels = levels_x
  )
}


has_event <- function(x) {

  x <- clean_text(x)

  !is.na(x) &
    x != "" &
    !x %in%
      c(
        "-",
        "na",
        "n/a",
        "none"
      )
}


fraction_n <- function(x) {

  x <- as.character(x)

  as.numeric(
    str_match(
      x,
      "(\\d+)\\s*/\\s*(\\d+)"
    )[, 2]
  )
}


fraction_den <- function(x) {

  x <- as.character(x)

  as.numeric(
    str_match(
      x,
      "(\\d+)\\s*/\\s*(\\d+)"
    )[, 3]
  )
}


# =============================================================================
# 3. GENERIC REPEATED-MEASUREMENT READER
# =============================================================================

read_measurement <- function(
  file,
  sheet_pattern,
  variable_name,
  value_patterns
) {

  sheet <- find_sheet(
    file,
    sheet_pattern
  )


  header_row <- find_header_row(
    file,
    sheet,
    c(
      "sheep|tag|animal|ewe|(^|\\s)id($|\\s)"
    )
  )


  x <- read_excel(
    file,
    sheet = sheet,
    skip = header_row - 1,
    col_types = "text"
  ) %>%
    clean_names()


  id_col <- pick_column(
    names(x),
    c(
      "^sheep$",
      "sheep_id",
      "^tag$",
      "tag_number",
      "tag_no",
      "^animal$",
      "^ewe$",
      "^id$"
    )
  )


  group_col <- pick_column(
    names(x),
    c(
      "^group$",
      "^dose$",
      "dose_ppm",
      "treatment"
    )
  )


  time_col <- pick_column(
    names(x),
    c(
      "^date$",
      "sample_date",
      "collection_date",
      "^month$",
      "^week$",
      "^time$",
      "time_point",
      "sampling",
      "visit"
    )
  )


  value_col <- pick_column(
    names(x),
    value_patterns
  )


  excluded <- c(
    id_col,
    group_col,
    time_col
  )

  excluded <- excluded[
    !is.na(excluded)
  ]


  # Fallback if measurement column name is unusual
  if (
    is.na(value_col) ||
    value_col %in% excluded
  ) {

    possible_values <- setdiff(
      names(x),
      excluded
    )


    numeric_fraction <- sapply(
      possible_values,
      function(v) {

        y <- suppressWarnings(
          parse_number(
            x[[v]]
          )
        )

        mean(
          !is.na(y)
        )
      }
    )


    value_col <- possible_values[
      which.max(
        numeric_fraction
      )
    ]
  }


  out <- x %>%

    transmute(

      sheep_id =
        clean_id(
          .data[[id_col]]
        ),

      group_raw =
        if (!is.na(group_col))
          .data[[group_col]]
        else
          NA_character_,

      time_raw =
        if (!is.na(time_col))
          as.character(
            .data[[time_col]]
          )
        else
          "1",

      value =
        suppressWarnings(
          parse_number(
            .data[[value_col]]
          )
        )
    ) %>%

    fill(
      group_raw,
      .direction = "down"
    ) %>%

    mutate(

      group =
        parse_group(
          group_raw
        ),

      variable =
        variable_name,

      source_sheet =
        sheet
    ) %>%

    filter(
      !is.na(sheep_id),
      !is.na(value)
    )


  out
}

s1_group_col <- pick_column(

study1_pg <- s1_pg_raw %>%

  transmute(

    sheep_id =

    group_raw =
      .data[[s1_group_col]],

    status =
      clean_text(
        .data[[s1_status_col]]
      )
  ) %>%

  fill(
    group_raw,
    .direction = "down"
  ) %>%

  mutate(

    group =
      parse_group(
        group_raw
      ),

    pregnant =
      case_when(

        str_detect(
          status,
          "^pg$|pregnant"
        ) ~
          1L,

        str_detect(
          status,
          "^open$"
        ) ~
          0L,

        TRUE ~
          NA_integer_
      )
  ) %>%

  filter(
    !is.na(sheep_id),
    sheep_id != STUDY1_EXCLUDE
  ) %>%

  distinct(
    sheep_id,
    .keep_all = TRUE
  )

)

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Helper function:
# remove any treatment group read from the measurement sheet and replace it
# with the authoritative treatment assignment from the pregnancy file.
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

attach_study1_group <- function(data) {

  data %>%

    select(
      -any_of("group")
    ) %>%

    left_join(
      study1_groups,
      by = "sheep_id"
    )
}


# Apply authoritative treatment groups

    s1_liver

  transmute(

      .data[[s1_cycle2_col]]
  ) %>%

  filter(
    !is.na(
      group
    )
  ) %>%

  mutate(

    repeat_cycle =
      fraction_n(
        cycle2_raw
      ),

    total =
      fraction_den(
        cycle2_raw
      ),

    no_repeat_cycle =
      total -
      repeat_cycle
  ) %>%

  filter(
    !is.na(
      repeat_cycle
    ),
    !is.na(
      total
    )
  )

# =============================================================================
# 9. STUDY 2 — INDIVIDUAL BREEDING / ULTRASOUND DATA
# =============================================================================

s2_raw <- read_excel(

  STUDY2_REPRO_FILE,

  sheet = "individual data",

  col_names = FALSE,

  col_types = "text",

  .name_repair = "minimal"
)


row_text <- apply(

  s2_raw,

  1,

  function(x) {

    clean_text(
      paste(
        x,
        collapse = " "
      )
    )
  }
)


s2_header_row <- which(

  str_detect(
    row_text,
    "group"
  ) &

  str_detect(
    row_text,
    "tag"
  ) &

  str_detect(
    row_text,
    "ultrasound"
  )

)[1]


if (is.na(s2_header_row)) {

  stop(
    "Could not identify Study 2 individual-data header."
  )
}


header1 <- as.character(
  s2_raw[
    s2_header_row,
  ]
)


header2 <- as.character(
  s2_raw[
    s2_header_row + 1,
  ]
)


new_names <- character(
  length(
    header1
  )
)


for (j in seq_along(header1)) {

  top <- clean_text(
    header1[j]
  )

  bottom <- clean_text(
    header2[j]
  )


  new_names[j] <- case_when(

    str_detect(
      top,
      "^group$"
    ) ~
      "group_raw",

    str_detect(
      top,
      "^pen$"
    ) ~
      "pen",

    str_detect(
      top,
      "tag"
    ) ~
      "sheep_id_raw",

    str_detect(
      top,
      "pessary"
    ) ~
      "pessary_out_raw",

    str_detect(
      bottom,
      "1st.*cycle"
    ) ~
      "bred_cycle_1_raw",

    str_detect(
      bottom,
      "2nd.*cycle"
    ) ~
      "bred_cycle_2_raw",

    str_detect(
      bottom,
      "3rd.*cycle"
    ) ~
      "bred_cycle_3_raw",

    str_detect(
      bottom,
      "4th.*cycle"
    ) ~
      "bred_cycle_4_raw",

    str_detect(
      top,
      "ultrasound.*1.?23"
    ) ~
      "ultrasound_1_raw",

    str_detect(
      top,
      "ultrasound.*3.?8"
    ) ~
      "ultrasound_2_raw",

    str_detect(
      top,
      "ultrasound.*5.?10"
    ) ~
      "ultrasound_3_raw",

    TRUE ~
      paste0(
        "unused_",
        j
      )
  )
}


study2_repro_raw <- s2_raw[

  (s2_header_row + 2):
    nrow(
      s2_raw
    ),

] %>%

  setNames(
    new_names
  ) %>%

  as_tibble()


study2_repro <- study2_repro_raw %>%

  mutate(

    sheep_id =
      clean_id(
        sheep_id_raw
      ),

    group_raw =
      as.character(
        group_raw
      )
  ) %>%

  fill(
    group_raw,
    .direction = "down"
  ) %>%

  mutate(

    group =
      parse_group(
        group_raw
      )
  ) %>%

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Only retain sheep appearing in Study#2_STATS.xlsx
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

  filter(
    sheep_id %in%
      study2_valid_ids
  ) %>%

  mutate(

    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Actual breeding-cycle participation
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------

    cycle1_present =
      has_event(
        bred_cycle_1_raw
      ),

    cycle2_present =
      has_event(
        bred_cycle_2_raw
      ),

    cycle3_present =
      has_event(
        bred_cycle_3_raw
      ),

    cycle4_present =
      has_event(
        bred_cycle_4_raw
      ),


    n_breeding_cycles =
      as.integer(
        cycle1_present
      ) +
      as.integer(
        cycle2_present
      ) +
      as.integer(
        cycle3_present
      ) +
      as.integer(
        cycle4_present
      ),


    repeat_breeding =
      case_when(

        n_breeding_cycles >= 1 ~
          as.integer(
            n_breeding_cycles > 1
          ),

        TRUE ~
          NA_integer_
      ),


    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Clean ultrasound results
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------

    us1 =
      clean_text(
        ultrasound_1_raw
      ),

    us2 =
      clean_text(
        ultrasound_2_raw
      ),

    us3 =
      clean_text(
        ultrasound_3_raw
      ),


    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Positive at first ultrasound
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------

    initial_positive =
      as.integer(

        str_detect(
          us1,
          "pregnant"
        )
      ),


    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # First ultrasound not positive,
    # but later ultrasound positive
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------

    later_positive =
      as.integer(

        !str_detect(
          us1,
          "pregnant"
        ) &

        (
          str_detect(
            us2,
            "pregnant"
          ) |

          str_detect(
            us3,
            "pregnant"
          )
        )
      ),


    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Final pregnancy classification
    #
    # Any documented pregnancy = pregnant
    #
    # Otherwise, any documented "open" result = open
    #
    # "-" or other indeterminate records remain NA unless another ultrasound
    # establishes pregnancy/open status.
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------

    ever_pregnant =
      case_when(

        str_detect(
          us1,
          "pregnant"
        ) |

        str_detect(
          us2,
          "pregnant"
        ) |

        str_detect(
          us3,
          "pregnant"
        ) ~
          1L,


        str_detect(

          str_c(
            us1,
            us2,
            us3,
            sep = " "
          ),

          "\\bopen\\b"
        ) ~
          0L,


        TRUE ~
          NA_integer_
      ),


    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Ultrasound-based reproductive category
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------

    efficiency_status =
      case_when(

        initial_positive == 1 ~
          "Initial positive",

        later_positive == 1 ~
          "Later positive",

        ever_pregnant == 0 ~
          "Open",

        TRUE ~
          "Unknown"
      )
  ) %>%

  distinct(
    sheep_id,
    .keep_all = TRUE
  )


study2_pg <- study2_repro %>%

    pregnant =

# =============================================================================
# STUDY 2 — STANDARDIZE BREEDING DATES
#
# IMPORTANT:
# The year entered in the reproductive workbook is only a placeholder.
# Month/day are the meaningful values.
#
# Study season:
#   Jul–Dec -> 2026
#   Jan–Jun -> 2027
# =============================================================================

parse_study2_breeding_date <- function(x) {

  x_chr <- str_trim(
    as.character(x)
  )


  x_chr[
    is.na(x_chr) |
    x_chr %in%
      c(
        "",
        "-",
        "NA",
        "N/A",
        "na",
        "n/a",
        "none"
      )
  ] <- NA_character_


  out <- as.Date(
    rep(
      NA_character_,
      length(x_chr)
    )
  )


  for (
    i in seq_along(
      x_chr
    )
  ) {

    if (
      is.na(
        x_chr[i]
      )
    ) {
      next
    }


    raw <- x_chr[i]


    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Try Excel serial date first
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------

    numeric_value <- suppressWarnings(
      as.numeric(
        raw
      )
    )


    temp_date <- as.Date(
      NA_character_
    )


    if (
      !is.na(
        numeric_value
      ) &&
      numeric_value > 20000 &&
      numeric_value < 80000
    ) {

      temp_date <- as.Date(
        numeric_value,
        origin = "1899-12-30"
      )

    } else {

      # -----------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Extract month/day from text.
      #
      # This intentionally ignores the recorded year because years in the
      # reproductive workbook are placeholders.
      # -----------------------------------------------------------------------

      md <- str_match(
        raw,
        "(\\d{1,2})[/-](\\d{1,2})"
      )


      if (
        !is.na(
          md[1, 1]
        )
      ) {

        month_num <- as.integer(
          md[1, 2]
        )

        day_num <- as.integer(
          md[1, 3]
        )


        study_year <- ifelse(
          month_num >= 7,
          2026,
          2027
        )


        temp_date <- suppressWarnings(
          as.Date(
            sprintf(
              "%04d-%02d-%02d",
              study_year,
              month_num,
              day_num
            )
          )
        )
      }
    }


    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Even if Excel supplied a complete date with a placeholder year,
    # retain only month/day and assign it to the correct study year.
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------

    if (
      !is.na(
        temp_date
      )
    ) {

      month_num <- as.integer(
        format(
          temp_date,
          "%m"
        )
      )

      day_num <- as.integer(
        format(
          temp_date,
          "%d"
        )
      )


      study_year <- ifelse(
        month_num >= 7,
        2026,
        2027
      )


      out[i] <- as.Date(
        sprintf(
          "%04d-%02d-%02d",
          study_year,
          month_num,
          day_num
        )
      )
    }
  }


  out
}

# =============================================================================
# 11. LONGITUDINAL Se MODEL
# =============================================================================

run_se_model <- function(
  data,
  groups,
  time_variable,
  title
) {

  x <- data %>%

    filter(
      group %in% groups,
      value > 0,
      !is.na(
        .data[[time_variable]]
      )
    ) %>%

    mutate(

      group =
        factor(
          group,
          levels = groups
        ),

      time_factor =
        ordered_factor(
          .data[[time_variable]]
        ),

      log_se =
        log(
          value
        )
    )


  model <- lmer(

    log_se ~
      group *
      time_factor +
      (1 | sheep_id),

    data = x,

    REML = FALSE
  )


  cat("\n============================================================\n")
  cat(title, "\n")
  cat("============================================================\n")


  result <- anova(
    model,
    type = 3
  )


  print(
    result
  )


  invisible(
    list(
      model = model,
      anova = result,
      data = x
    )
  )
}

# =============================================================================
# STUDY 1 — TEMPORAL Se CONCENTRATION SUMMARIES
#
# These summaries remain in the ORIGINAL Se concentration units.
# They are descriptive summaries and are separate from the
# log-transformed mixed-effects models.
# =============================================================================


summarize_temporal_se <- function(data) {

  data %>%

    filter(
      !is.na(value),
      value > 0,
      !is.na(group),
      !is.na(time_raw)
    ) %>%

    mutate(

      time_num =
        suppressWarnings(
          parse_number(
            as.character(time_raw)
          )
        )
    ) %>%

    group_by(
      group,
      time_raw,
      time_num
    ) %>%

    summarise(

      n_ewe =
        n_distinct(
          sheep_id
        ),

      n_obs =
        n(),

      mean_se =
        mean(
          value,
          na.rm = TRUE
        ),

      sd_se =
        sd(
          value,
          na.rm = TRUE
        ),

      se_se =
        sd_se /
        sqrt(
          n_obs
        ),

      median_se =
        median(
          value,
          na.rm = TRUE
        ),

      min_se =
        min(
          value,
          na.rm = TRUE
        ),

      max_se =
        max(
          value,
          na.rm = TRUE
        ),

      .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%

    arrange(
      group,
      time_num,
      time_raw
    )
}

        "Initial positive",
        "Later positive",
        "Open"
      )
  )
)

)

# =============================================================================
# 19. BASELINE BODY WEIGHT
#
# Identify the earliest available body-weight measurement for each ewe.
# =============================================================================

get_baseline_weight <- function(
  data,
  time_variable
) {

  data %>%

    filter(
      !is.na(
        .data[[time_variable]]
      )
    ) %>%

    arrange(
      sheep_id,
      .data[[time_variable]]
    ) %>%

    group_by(
      sheep_id
    ) %>%

    slice(
      1
    ) %>%

    ungroup() %>%

    transmute(

      sheep_id,

      baseline_weight =
        value
    )
}


# Study 1
s1_baseline_weight <- get_baseline_weight(
  s1_weight,
  "time_raw"
)


# Study 2
s2_baseline_weight <- get_baseline_weight(
  s2_weight,
  "sample_date"
)



# =============================================================================
# 20. BASELINE BODY WEIGHT CHECK
#
# Two questions are evaluated:
#
# 1. Did baseline body weight differ among treatment groups?
#
# 2. Was baseline body weight associated with final pregnancy outcome?
#
# Baseline weight is standardized before the pregnancy model so that the
# coefficient represents a one-standard-deviation increase in body weight.
# =============================================================================

run_weight_check <- function(
  pregnancy_data,
  baseline_weight,
  groups,
  title
) {

  x <- pregnancy_data %>%

    filter(
      group %in% groups,
      !is.na(
        pregnant
      )
    ) %>%

    left_join(
      baseline_weight,
      by = "sheep_id"
    ) %>%

    filter(
      !is.na(
        baseline_weight
      )
    ) %>%

    mutate(

      group =
        factor(
          group,
          levels = groups
        ),

      weight_z =
        as.numeric(
          scale(
            baseline_weight
          )
        )
    )


  cat("\n============================================================\n")
  cat(title, "\n")
  cat("============================================================\n")


  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Did treatment groups differ in baseline body weight?
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

  baseline_model <- lm(

    baseline_weight ~
      group,

    data = x
  )


  cat("\nBASELINE WEIGHT BY TREATMENT\n\n")

  print(
    anova(
      baseline_model
    )
  )


  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Was baseline body weight associated with final pregnancy?
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

  pregnancy_model <- glm(

    pregnant ~
      weight_z,

    data = x,

    family =
      binomial(),

    method =
      brglm2::brglmFit,

    type =
      "AS_mean"
  )


  cat("\nBASELINE WEIGHT -> FINAL PREGNANCY\n\n")

  print(
    coef(
      summary(
        pregnancy_model
      )
    )
  )


  invisible(
    list(
      baseline_model = baseline_model,
      pregnancy_model = pregnancy_model,
      data = x
    )
  )
}

# Study 1
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

  study1_pg,

  s1_baseline_weight,

  c(

  "STUDY 1 — BASELINE WEIGHT"

# =============================================================================
# 21. LONGITUDINAL BODY WEIGHT
#
# Evaluate whether body-weight trajectories differed among treatment groups
# over time.
#
# This is NOT a simple baseline-to-final change score.
#
# Treatment, time, and treatment × time are fixed effects.
# Ewe is included as a random intercept to account for repeated measurements.
# =============================================================================

run_weight_longitudinal <- function(
  data,
  groups,
  time_variable,
  title
) {

  x <- data %>%

    filter(
      group %in% groups,
      !is.na(
        .data[[time_variable]]
      ),
      !is.na(
        value
      )
    ) %>%

    mutate(

      group =
        factor(
          group,
          levels = groups
        ),

      time_factor =
        ordered_factor(
          .data[[time_variable]]
        )
    )


  model <- lmer(

    value ~
      group *
      time_factor +
      (1 | sheep_id),

    data = x,

    REML = FALSE
  )


  cat("\n============================================================\n")
  cat(title, "\n")
  cat("============================================================\n")


  print(
    anova(
      model,
      type = 3
    )
  )


  invisible(
    model
  )
}

  "STUDY 1 — WEIGHT OVER TIME"

# =============================================================================
# 21A. STUDY 1 — BASELINE-TO-FINAL BODY WEIGHT CHANGE
#
# This analysis directly evaluates change in body weight.
#
# For each ewe:
#
#   Weight change = final available weight - baseline weight
#
# Positive value = weight gain
# Negative value = weight loss
#
# This analysis is separate from the longitudinal mixed-effects model above.
# =============================================================================


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Prepare Study 1 weight data
#
# Study 1 weight time_raw values are Excel serial dates.
# Convert them to actual calendar dates before identifying the first and
# last measurements.
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

study1_weight_dated <- s1_weight %>%

  filter(
    group %in%
      c(
        "Control",
        "10 ppm",
        "30 ppm",
        "60 ppm"
      ),
    !is.na(
      value
    ),
    !is.na(
      time_raw
    )
  ) %>%

  mutate(

    weight_date =
      parse_mixed_date(
        time_raw
      )
  ) %>%

  filter(
    !is.na(
      weight_date
    )
  )



# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Calculate baseline-to-final change for each ewe
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

study1_weight_change <- study1_weight_dated %>%

  arrange(
    sheep_id,
    weight_date
  ) %>%

  group_by(
    sheep_id
  ) %>%

  summarise(

    group =
      first(
        group
      ),

    baseline_date =
      first(
        weight_date
      ),

    final_date =
      last(
        weight_date
      ),

    baseline_weight =
      first(
        value
      ),

    final_weight =
      last(
        value
      ),

    n_weight_measurements =
      n(),

    weight_change =
      final_weight -
      baseline_weight,

    percent_weight_change =
      100 *
      (
        final_weight -
        baseline_weight
      ) /
      baseline_weight,

    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%

  filter(
    n_weight_measurements >= 2
  ) %>%

  mutate(

    group =
      factor(
        group,
        levels =
          c(
            "Control",
            "10 ppm",
            "30 ppm",
            "60 ppm"
          )
      )
  )



# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Print individual ewe results
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

cat("\n============================================================\n")
cat("STUDY 1 — INDIVIDUAL BODY WEIGHT CHANGE\n")
cat("============================================================\n\n")


print(
  study1_weight_change,
  n = Inf
)



# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Descriptive summary by treatment group
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

study1_weight_change_summary <- study1_weight_change %>%

  group_by(
    group
  ) %>%

  summarise(

    n =
      n(),

    mean_baseline_weight =
      mean(
        baseline_weight,
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),

    sd_baseline_weight =
      sd(
        baseline_weight,
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),

    mean_final_weight =
      mean(
        final_weight,
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),

    sd_final_weight =
      sd(
        final_weight,
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),

    mean_weight_change =
      mean(
        weight_change,
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),

    sd_weight_change =
      sd(
        weight_change,
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),

    median_weight_change =
      median(
        weight_change,
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),

    mean_percent_weight_change =
      mean(
        percent_weight_change,
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),

    .groups = "drop"
  )

# =============================================================================
# 21B. STUDY 1 — BASELINE BODY WEIGHT VS WHOLE-BLOOD Se
#
# Zane's question:
# "Did you do body weight versus selenium concentration or did you look at
#  change in body weight?"
#
# Section 21A evaluates CHANGE IN BODY WEIGHT.
#
# This section evaluates the relationship between baseline body weight and
# measured whole-blood Se concentration at the first sampling occasion.
#
# Month 1 whole-blood Se is used so that a single Se concentration is
# represented for each ewe. This avoids incorrectly pairing the weight dates
# with Se sampling months, because the two datasets use different time scales.
#
# Se is natural-log transformed, consistent with the other Se analyses.
# =============================================================================


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Extract Month 1 whole-blood Se for each ewe
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

study1_month1_se <- s1_blood %>%

  mutate(

    month =
      suppressWarnings(
        as.numeric(
          time_raw
        )
      )
  ) %>%

  filter(
    month == 1,
    value > 0,
    !is.na(
      value
    )
  ) %>%

  group_by(
    sheep_id
  ) %>%

  summarise(

    baseline_se =
      mean(
        value,
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),

    .groups = "drop"
  )



# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Join baseline body weight with Month 1 Se
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

study1_weight_se_baseline <- s1_baseline_weight %>%

  inner_join(
    study1_month1_se,
    by = "sheep_id"
  ) %>%

  mutate(

    log_baseline_se =
      log(
        baseline_se
      )
  )



cat("\n============================================================\n")
cat("STUDY 1 — BASELINE BODY WEIGHT VS MONTH 1 WHOLE-BLOOD Se\n")
cat("============================================================\n\n")


cat(
  "Number of ewes:",
  nrow(
    study1_weight_se_baseline
  ),
  "\n\n"
)


print(
  study1_weight_se_baseline,
  n = Inf
)



# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Linear regression
#
# Question:
# Is baseline body weight associated with measured Month 1 whole-blood Se?
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

study1_weight_se_baseline_model <- lm(

  baseline_weight ~
    log_baseline_se,

  data =
    study1_weight_se_baseline
)



cat("\nLINEAR REGRESSION\n\n")


print(
  summary(
    study1_weight_se_baseline_model
  )
)



# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. ANOVA table for the Se association
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

study1_weight_se_baseline_anova <- anova(
  study1_weight_se_baseline_model
)



cat("\nANOVA — BASELINE BODY WEIGHT VS MONTH 1 WHOLE-BLOOD Se\n\n")


print(
  study1_weight_se_baseline_anova
)



# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Pearson correlation
#
# Included as a descriptive measure of the strength and direction of the
# relationship. The regression above is the primary inferential analysis.
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

study1_weight_se_baseline_cor <- cor.test(

  study1_weight_se_baseline$baseline_weight,

# =============================================================================
# 22. STUDY 1 — WHOLE BLOOD Se AND FINAL PREGNANCY
#
# Two complementary analyses are performed:
#
# A. REPRODUCTIVE-WINDOW ANALYSIS
#    Months 1–3 only.
#
#    Biological timeline:
#       Cycle 1 = week 7
#       Cycle 2 = week 10
#       Se supplementation stopped = week 12
#
#    Thus, months 1–3 represent the period during which active Se
#    supplementation and breeding overlapped.
#
#    This is the PRIMARY supporting analysis for interpreting the
#    relationship between Whole Blood Se and reproduction.
#
#
# B. FULL-TRAJECTORY ANALYSIS
#    Months 1–15.
#
#    This describes whether pregnant and open ewes followed different
#    Se trajectories over the complete supplementation + follow-up period.
#
#    This is SECONDARY and should not be interpreted as evidence that
#    late post-breeding Se concentrations caused reproductive outcome.
# =============================================================================


# =============================================================================
# 22A. BUILD COMMON STUDY 1 OUTCOME DATA
# =============================================================================

study1_outcome_se_all <- s1_blood %>%

  left_join(

    study1_pg %>%

      filter(
        !is.na(
          pregnant
        )
      ) %>%

      transmute(

        sheep_id,

        reproductive_status =
          if_else(
            pregnant == 1,
            "Pregnant",
            "Open"
          )
      ),

    by = "sheep_id"
  ) %>%

  mutate(

    # Study 1 time_raw values are MONTHS
    month =
      suppressWarnings(
        as.numeric(
          time_raw
        )
      ),

    reproductive_status =
      factor(
        reproductive_status,
        levels =
          c(
            "Pregnant",
            "Open"
          )
      ),

    log_se =
      log(
        value
      )
  ) %>%

  filter(

    !is.na(
      reproductive_status
    ),

    !is.na(
      month
    ),

    value > 0
  )


# =============================================================================
# 22B. PRIMARY SUPPORTING ANALYSIS:
#      REPRODUCTIVE WINDOW — MONTHS 1–3
#
# Cycle 1 = week 7
# Cycle 2 = week 10
# Feed stopped = week 12
# =============================================================================

study1_repro_window_se <- study1_outcome_se_all %>%

  filter(
    month >= 1,
    month <= 3
  ) %>%

  mutate(

    month_factor =
      factor(
        month,
        levels =
          sort(
            unique(
              month
            )
          )
      )
  )


study1_repro_window_model <- lmer(

  log_se ~
    reproductive_status *
    month_factor +
    (1 | sheep_id),

  data =
    study1_repro_window_se,

  REML =
    FALSE
)


cat("\n============================================================\n")
cat("STUDY 1 — WHOLE BLOOD Se DURING REPRODUCTIVE WINDOW\n")
cat("MONTHS 1–3\n")
cat("Cycle 1 = Week 7 | Cycle 2 = Week 10 | Feed stopped = Week 12\n")
cat("============================================================\n")


study1_repro_window_anova <- anova(

  type = 3
)


print(
  study1_repro_window_anova
)

      ),

    mean_se =

        value,
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),

    sd_se =

        value,

      ),

    median_se =
```

```{r}
# =============================================================================
# 26. FINAL MANUSCRIPT REPORT
#
# PURPOSE
#   1. Collect all final statistical tests
#   2. Print H0 and H1
#   3. Print p-values
#   4. Print REJECT / FAIL TO REJECT H0
#   5. Print concise manuscript interpretation
#   6. Print descriptive reproductive summaries
#   7. Print baseline-weight summaries
#   8. Run secondary Control-vs-treatment Fisher contrasts
#   9. Save manuscript-ready CSV files
#  10. Save a complete TXT report
#
# IMPORTANT
#   This section assumes all models/tests above have already run successfully.
# =============================================================================


# =============================================================================
# 26.1 SETTINGS
# =============================================================================

ALPHA <- 0.05


FINAL_REPORT_DIR <- file.path(
  BASE_DIR,
  "Sheep_Final_Report"
)


dir.create(
  FINAL_REPORT_DIR,
  recursive = TRUE,
  showWarnings = FALSE
)


FINAL_REPORT_FILE <- file.path(
  FINAL_REPORT_DIR,
  "Final_Statistical_Report.txt"
)


# =============================================================================
# 26.2 HELPER FUNCTIONS
# =============================================================================


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Format p-values
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

format_p <- function(p) {

  if (
    length(p) == 0 ||
    is.na(p)
  ) {

    return(
      "NA"
    )
  }


  if (p < 0.0001) {

    return(
      format(
        p,
        scientific = TRUE,
        digits = 3
      )
    )
  }


  sprintf(
    "%.4f",
    p
  )
}


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Formal statistical decision
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

decision_from_p <- function(
  p,
  alpha = ALPHA
) {

  if (
    length(p) == 0 ||
    is.na(p)
  ) {

    return(
      "NOT EVALUATED"
    )
  }


  if (p < alpha) {

    "REJECT H0"

  } else {

    "FAIL TO REJECT H0"
  }
}


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Extract p-value from ANOVA table
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

extract_anova_p <- function(
  anova_object,
  term
) {

  x <- as.data.frame(
    anova_object
  )


  rn <- rownames(
    x
  )


  hit <- which(
    rn == term
  )


  if (length(hit) == 0) {

    warning(
      paste(
        "Term not found:",
        term
      )
    )

    return(
      NA_real_
    )
  }


  p_col <- grep(
    "^Pr\\(",
    names(x),
    value = TRUE
  )


  if (length(p_col) == 0) {

    warning(
      paste(
        "No p-value column found for:",
        term
      )
    )

    return(
      NA_real_
    )
  }


  as.numeric(
    x[
      hit[1],
      p_col[1]
    ]
  )
}


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Extract coefficient p-value
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

extract_coefficient_p <- function(
  model,
  term
) {

  x <- coef(
    summary(
      model
    )
  )


  if (
    !term %in%
      rownames(x)
  ) {

    return(
      NA_real_
    )
  }


  p_col <- grep(
    "^Pr\\(",
    colnames(x),
    value = TRUE
  )


  if (length(p_col) == 0) {

    return(
      NA_real_
    )
  }


  as.numeric(
    x[
      term,
      p_col[1]
    ]
  )
}


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Build one hypothesis-test row
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

make_test_row <- function(
  study,
  priority,
  analysis,
  term,
  p_value,
  h0,
  h1,
  reject_interpretation,
  fail_interpretation,
  note = NA_character_
) {

  decision <- decision_from_p(
    p_value
  )


  interpretation <- if (
    identical(
      decision,
      "REJECT H0"
    )
  ) {

    reject_interpretation

  } else if (
    identical(
      decision,
      "FAIL TO REJECT H0"
    )
  ) {

    fail_interpretation

  } else {

    "No statistical interpretation available."
  }


  tibble(

    study =
      study,

    priority =
      priority,

    analysis =
      analysis,

    term =
      term,

    h0 =
      h0,

    h1 =
      h1,

    p_value =
      p_value,

    decision =
      decision,

    interpretation =
      interpretation,

    note =
      note
  )
}

study1_final_summary <- study1_pg %>%

      pregnant

  ) %>%

  ) %>%

  summarise(

    final_n =
      n(),

    pregnant_n =
      sum(
        pregnant == 1
      ),

    open_n =
      sum(
        pregnant == 0
      ),

    pregnancy_percent =
      100 *
      pregnant_n /
      final_n,

    .groups =
      "drop"
  )


study1_reproductive_summary <- study1_repeat %>%

  mutate(
    group =
      as.character(
        group
      )
  ) %>%

  select(

    group,

    breeding_n =
      total,

    repeat_cycle_n =
      repeat_cycle,

    no_repeat_cycle_n =
      no_repeat_cycle

  ) %>%

  left_join(

    study1_final_summary %>%

      mutate(
        group =
          as.character(
            group
          )
      ),

    by =
      "group"
  ) %>%

    repeat_cycle_percent =
      100 *

      breeding_n
  ) %>%

  select(

    group,

    breeding_n,

    repeat_cycle_n,

    repeat_cycle_percent,

    final_n,

    pregnant_n,

    open_n,

    pregnancy_percent
  )

      ),

      ),

      sum(
        repeat_breeding == 0,

    repeat_breeding_percent =

    initial_positive_n =

    pregnancy_percent =

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Individual binary outcome
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

pairwise_binary_vs_control <- function(
  data,
  group_col,
  outcome_col,
  doses
) {

  out <- lapply(

    doses,

    function(dose) {

      dat <- data %>%

        filter(
          as.character(
            .data[[group_col]]
          ) %in%
            c(
              "Control",
              dose
            ),

          !is.na(
            .data[[outcome_col]]
          )
        )


      tab <- table(

        factor(
          as.character(
            dat[[group_col]]
          ),
          levels =
            c(
              "Control",
              dose
            )
        ),

        factor(
          dat[[outcome_col]],
          levels =
            c(
              0,
              1
            )
        )
      )


      test <- fisher.test(
        tab
      )


      tibble(

        comparison =
          paste(
            "Control vs",
            dose
          ),

        p_value =
          test$p.value
      )
    }
  ) %>%

    bind_rows() %>%

    mutate(

      p_holm =
        p.adjust(
          p_value,
          method = "holm"
        ),

      decision_raw =
        if_else(
          p_value < ALPHA,
          "REJECT H0",
          "FAIL TO REJECT H0"
        ),

      decision_holm =
        if_else(
          p_holm < ALPHA,
          "REJECT H0",
          "FAIL TO REJECT H0"
        )
    )


  out
}


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Aggregated Study 1 repeat-cycle data
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

pairwise_repeat_study1 <- function(
  data
) {

  doses <- c(
    "10 ppm",
    "30 ppm",
    "60 ppm"
  )


  result <- lapply(

    doses,

    function(dose) {

      control <- data %>%
        filter(
          group == "Control"
        )


      treated <- data %>%
        filter(
          group == dose
        )


      tab <- rbind(

        Control =
          c(
            No_repeat =
              control$no_repeat_cycle,
            Repeat =
              control$repeat_cycle
          ),

        Treatment =
          c(
            No_repeat =
              treated$no_repeat_cycle,
            Repeat =
              treated$repeat_cycle
          )
      )


      test <- fisher.test(
        tab
      )


      tibble(

        comparison =
          paste(
            "Control vs",
            dose
          ),

        p_value =
          test$p.value
      )
    }
  ) %>%

    bind_rows() %>%

    mutate(

      p_holm =
        p.adjust(
          p_value,
          method = "holm"
        ),

      decision_raw =
        if_else(
          p_value < ALPHA,
          "REJECT H0",
          "FAIL TO REJECT H0"
        ),

      decision_holm =
        if_else(
          p_holm < ALPHA,
          "REJECT H0",
          "FAIL TO REJECT H0"
        )
    )


  result
}

print_final_report <- function() {


  sink(
    FINAL_REPORT_FILE,
    split = TRUE
  )


  on.exit(
    sink(),
    add = TRUE
  )


  cat("\n")
  cat("====================================================================\n")
  cat("FINAL SHEEP SELENIUM / REPRODUCTION STATISTICAL REPORT\n")
  cat("====================================================================\n")
  cat("\n")

  cat(
    "Alpha:",
    ALPHA,
    "\n"
  )

  cat(
    "Report directory:",
    FINAL_REPORT_DIR,
    "\n\n"
  )


  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Primary / secondary tests
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

  for (
    i in seq_len(
      nrow(
        final_tests
      )
    )
  ) {


    r <- final_tests[
      i,
    ]


    cat("\n")
    cat("--------------------------------------------------------------------\n")

    cat(
      r$study,
      " — ",
      r$analysis,
      "\n",
      sep = ""
    )

    cat(
      "Priority: ",
      r$priority,
      "\n",
      sep = ""
    )

    cat(
      "Term: ",
      r$term,
      "\n",
      sep = ""
    )

    cat("--------------------------------------------------------------------\n")


    cat(
      "H0: ",
      r$h0,
      "\n",
      sep = ""
    )


    cat(
      "H1: ",
      r$h1,
      "\n",
      sep = ""
    )


    cat(
      "p-value: ",
      format_p(
        r$p_value
      ),
      "\n",
      sep = ""
    )


    cat(
      "Decision: ",
      r$decision,
      "\n",
      sep = ""
    )


    cat(
      "Interpretation: ",
      r$interpretation,
      "\n",
      sep = ""
    )


    if (
      !is.na(
        r$note
      )
    ) {

      cat(
        "Note: ",

      )
    }
  }


  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

  cat("STUDY 1 — REPRODUCTIVE OUTCOME SUMMARY\n")

  cat("====================================================================\n")
  cat("BASELINE BODY-WEIGHT SUMMARY\n")
  cat("====================================================================\n\n")

  )


  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Pairwise Study 1 repeat breeding
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

  cat("\n\n")
  cat("====================================================================\n")
  cat("STUDY 1 — CONTROL CONTRASTS: REPEAT BREEDING\n")
  cat("====================================================================\n\n")

  )


  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

  )

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

  cat("====================================================================\n")
  cat("STUDY 2 — CONTROL CONTRASTS: FINAL PREGNANCY\n")
  cat("====================================================================\n\n")

  )


  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # QC
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

  cat("\n\n")
  cat("====================================================================\n")
  cat("STUDY 2 — COHORT QUALITY CONTROL\n")
  cat("====================================================================\n\n")

  print(
    study2_qc_summary,
    n = Inf
  )


  cat("\nStats IDs without matching reproductive records:\n")

  print(
    study2_ids_stats_not_repro
  )


  cat("\nExtra reproductive IDs excluded because they were absent from Study#2_STATS.xlsx:\n")

  print(
    study2_ids_repro_not_stats
  )


  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Interpretation notes
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

  cat("\n\n")
  cat("====================================================================\n")
  cat("IMPORTANT MANUSCRIPT INTERPRETATION NOTES\n")
  cat("====================================================================\n\n")


  cat(
    "1. A significant treatment × time interaction means that the effect of\n",
    "   treatment on Se or weight changes over time. In those cases, the\n",
    "   interaction and longitudinal trajectories should receive greater\n",
    "   emphasis than a single averaged treatment main effect.\n\n",
    sep = ""
  )


  cat(
    "2. Study 2 actual breeding-cycle records are the preferred measure of\n",
    "   breeding efficiency. Ultrasound timing is retained as a secondary\n",
    "   reproductive-outcome measure and should not be interpreted as exact\n",
    "   conception-cycle timing.\n\n",
    sep = ""
  )


  cat(
    "3. Outcome-stratified Whole Blood Se models are SUPPORTING, UNADJUSTED\n",
    "   associations. Reproductive-window models use only Se measurements\n",
    "   collected during the biologically relevant breeding/exposure period.\n",
    "   Full-follow-up outcome models are SECONDARY descriptions and include\n",
    "   post-breeding/post-supplementation measurements. Neither analysis\n",
    "   independently establishes that measured blood Se itself is the sole\n",
    "   causal mechanism.\n\n",
    sep = ""
  )


  cat(
    "4. Baseline body weight is the appropriate weight variable for assessing\n",
    "   whether pre-existing size differences could explain reproduction.\n",
    "   Post-treatment weight may itself respond to treatment and is therefore\n",
    "   analyzed as a secondary longitudinal outcome rather than automatically\n",
    "   adjusted away as a confounder.\n\n",
    sep = ""
  )


  cat(
    "5. Global exact tests are treated as the primary reproductive-outcome\n",
    "   tests. Control-vs-treatment comparisons are secondary contrasts.\n",
    "   Both raw and Holm-adjusted p-values are provided for those contrasts.\n\n",
    sep = ""
  )


  cat(
    "6. A result with p >= 0.05 is described as 'no statistically significant\n",
    "   evidence' rather than as proof of no biological effect. This distinction\n",
    "   is particularly important because sample sizes are small.\n\n",
    sep = ""
  )


  cat(
    "7. Sheep 8583 remains excluded from Study 1 individual pregnancy analyses\n",
    "   because its recorded pregnancy status is ambiguous.\n\n",
    sep = ""
  )


  cat("\n")
  cat("====================================================================\n")
  cat("FILES WRITTEN\n")
  cat("====================================================================\n\n")

  cat(
    "Full report:\n",
    FINAL_REPORT_FILE,

  cat(

    ),

  )


  invisible(

  )
```

```{r}
clean_time_numeric <- function(x) {

  x_chr <- as.character(x)

  out <- suppressWarnings(
    parse_number(x_chr)
  )

  out
}


make_se_summary <- function(
  data,
  time_var
) {

  data %>%

    filter(
      !is.na(group),
      !is.na(value),
      value > 0,
      !is.na(.data[[time_var]])
    ) %>%

    group_by(
      group,
      .data[[time_var]]
    ) %>%

    summarise(

      n =
        n(),

      mean_se =
        mean(
          value,
          na.rm = TRUE
        ),

      sd_se =
        sd(
          value,
          na.rm = TRUE
        ),

      se_se =
        sd_se /
        sqrt(n),

      .groups =
        "drop"
    )
}
```

```{r}
# ============================================================
# FINAL STUDY 2 REPRODUCTIVE OUTCOME CHECK
# Corrected Control cohort = 10 ewes
# ============================================================

set.seed(42)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. ENTER FINAL VERIFIED COUNTS
# ------------------------------------------------------------

# Repeat breeding
# Rows = treatment groups
# Columns = Repeat breeding, One cycle
repeat_breeding <- matrix(
  c(
    0, 10,   # Control
    5,  5,   # 10 ppm
    4,  6    # 30 ppm
  ),
  nrow = 3,
  byrow = TRUE,
  dimnames = list(
    Group = c("Control", "10 ppm", "30 ppm"),
    Outcome = c("Repeat", "One_cycle")
  )
)

# Final pregnancy
# Columns = Pregnant, Open
final_pregnancy <- matrix(
  c(
    10, 0,   # Control
     9, 1,   # 10 ppm
     6, 4    # 30 ppm
  ),
  nrow = 3,
  byrow = TRUE,
  dimnames = list(
    Group = c("Control", "10 ppm", "30 ppm"),
    Outcome = c("Pregnant", "Open")
  )
)


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. PRINT TABLES
# ------------------------------------------------------------

cat("\n============================================================\n")
cat("STUDY 2 FINAL DATA CHECK\n")
cat("============================================================\n")

cat("\nREPEAT BREEDING COUNTS\n")
print(repeat_breeding)

cat("\nFINAL PREGNANCY COUNTS\n")
print(final_pregnancy)


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. GLOBAL FISHER EXACT TESTS
#    Monte Carlo version matching manuscript approach
# ------------------------------------------------------------

set.seed(42)

repeat_global <- fisher.test(
  repeat_breeding,
  simulate.p.value = TRUE,
  B = 100000
)

set.seed(42)

pregnancy_global <- fisher.test(
  final_pregnancy,
  simulate.p.value = TRUE,
  B = 100000
)

cat("\n============================================================\n")
cat("GLOBAL TESTS\n")
cat("============================================================\n")

cat(
  "\nOne cycle vs repeat breeding:\n",
  "P = ", format.pval(repeat_global$p.value, digits = 6), "\n",
  sep = ""
)

cat(
  "\nFinal pregnancy:\n",
  "P = ", format.pval(pregnancy_global$p.value, digits = 6), "\n",
  sep = ""
)


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. PAIRWISE CONTROL VS TREATMENT
# ------------------------------------------------------------

# ---- Repeat breeding ----

repeat_control_10 <- fisher.test(
  repeat_breeding[c("Control", "10 ppm"), ]
)

repeat_control_30 <- fisher.test(
  repeat_breeding[c("Control", "30 ppm"), ]
)

repeat_raw <- c(
  "Control vs 10 ppm" = repeat_control_10$p.value,
  "Control vs 30 ppm" = repeat_control_30$p.value
)

repeat_holm <- p.adjust(
  repeat_raw,
  method = "holm"
)


# ---- Final pregnancy ----

preg_control_10 <- fisher.test(
  final_pregnancy[c("Control", "10 ppm"), ]
)

preg_control_30 <- fisher.test(
  final_pregnancy[c("Control", "30 ppm"), ]
)

preg_raw <- c(
  "Control vs 10 ppm" = preg_control_10$p.value,
  "Control vs 30 ppm" = preg_control_30$p.value
)

preg_holm <- p.adjust(
  preg_raw,
  method = "holm"
)


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. BUILD FINAL RESULTS TABLES
# ------------------------------------------------------------

repeat_results <- data.frame(
  Comparison = names(repeat_raw),
  P_raw = as.numeric(repeat_raw),
  P_Holm = as.numeric(repeat_holm)
)

pregnancy_results <- data.frame(
  Comparison = names(preg_raw),
  P_raw = as.numeric(preg_raw),
  P_Holm = as.numeric(preg_holm)
)


cat("\n============================================================\n")
cat("REPEAT BREEDING — CONTROL CONTRASTS\n")
cat("============================================================\n")

print(
  repeat_results,
  row.names = FALSE
)


cat("\n============================================================\n")
cat("FINAL PREGNANCY — CONTROL CONTRASTS\n")
cat("============================================================\n")

print(
  pregnancy_results,
  row.names = FALSE
)


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 6. PERCENTAGES FOR MANUSCRIPT
# ------------------------------------------------------------

repeat_percent <- 100 * repeat_breeding[, "Repeat"] /
  rowSums(repeat_breeding)

pregnancy_percent <- 100 * final_pregnancy[, "Pregnant"] /
  rowSums(final_pregnancy)

summary_table <- data.frame(
  Group = rownames(repeat_breeding),

  Repeat_n =
    repeat_breeding[, "Repeat"],

  Repeat_total =
    rowSums(repeat_breeding),

  Repeat_percent =
    repeat_percent,

  Pregnant_n =
    final_pregnancy[, "Pregnant"],

  Pregnancy_total =
    rowSums(final_pregnancy),

  Pregnancy_percent =
    pregnancy_percent
)

cat("\n============================================================\n")
cat("FINAL STUDY 2 REPRODUCTIVE SUMMARY\n")
cat("============================================================\n")

print(
  summary_table,
  row.names = FALSE
)


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 7. FINAL SANITY CHECKS
# ------------------------------------------------------------

stopifnot(
  rowSums(repeat_breeding)["Control"] == 10,
  repeat_breeding["Control", "Repeat"] == 0,
  repeat_breeding["Control", "One_cycle"] == 10,

  rowSums(final_pregnancy)["Control"] == 10,
  final_pregnancy["Control", "Pregnant"] == 10,
  final_pregnancy["Control", "Open"] == 0,

  rowSums(repeat_breeding)["10 ppm"] == 10,
  rowSums(repeat_breeding)["30 ppm"] == 10,

  rowSums(final_pregnancy)["10 ppm"] == 10,
  rowSums(final_pregnancy)["30 ppm"] == 10
)

cat("\n============================================================\n")
cat("SANITY CHECK PASSED: ALL STUDY 2 GROUPS CONTAIN 10 EWES\n")
cat("============================================================\n")
```

```{r}
# =============================================================================
# FINAL CLEAN PUBLICATION FIGURES
#
# FIGURE 1:
#   Whole Blood Se ONLY
#
#   Two versions are created:
#     1. Y-axis labeled in ppm
#     2. Y-axis labeled in mg/kg
#
#   For each unit version:
#     A. WITH individual ewe trajectories
#     B. MEANS ± SE ONLY
#
#   Study 1 = Panel A
#   Study 2 = Panel B
#
#   No Study 1 / Study 2 titles printed above individual panels.
#   Panel labels A and B distinguish the studies.
# =============================================================================


library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(patchwork)
library(ragg)
library(scales)
library(readr)


# =============================================================================
# 1. COLOR-BLIND-SAFE PALETTE
# =============================================================================

treatment_colors <- c(
  "Control" = "#000000",
  "10 ppm"  = "#0072B2",
  "30 ppm"  = "#E69F00",
  "60 ppm"  = "#CC79A7"
)


treatment_shapes <- c(
  "Control" = 16,
  "10 ppm"  = 17,
  "30 ppm"  = 15,
  "60 ppm"  = 18
)


treatment_linetypes <- c(
  "Control" = "solid",
  "10 ppm"  = "dashed",
  "30 ppm"  = "dotdash",
  "60 ppm"  = "longdash"
)


# =============================================================================
# 2. PUBLICATION THEME
# =============================================================================

theme_publication <- function() {

  theme_classic(
    base_size = 11,
    base_family = "Times New Roman"
  ) +

    theme(

      text =
        element_text(
          family = "Times New Roman",
          color = "black"
        ),

      plot.title =
        element_text(
          family = "Times New Roman",
          size = 13,
          face = "bold",
          hjust = 0,
          margin = margin(
            b = 8
          )
        ),

      axis.title =
        element_text(
          family = "Times New Roman",
          size = 11,
          face = "bold"
        ),

      axis.text =
        element_text(
          family = "Times New Roman",
          size = 10,
          color = "black"
        ),

      legend.title =
        element_text(
          family = "Times New Roman",
          size = 10,
          face = "bold"
        ),

      legend.text =
        element_text(
          family = "Times New Roman",
          size = 10
        ),

      strip.background =
        element_blank(),

      strip.text =
        element_text(
          family = "Times New Roman",
          size = 11,
          face = "bold"
        ),

      panel.grid =
        element_blank(),

      plot.margin =
        margin(
          8,
          10,
          8,
          8
        )
    )
}


# =============================================================================
# 3. CREATE STUDY 1 WHOLE-BLOOD PUBLICATION DATA 
# =============================================================================
#
# IMPORTANT:
# This creates the missing s1_blood_pub object.
#
# Study 1 uses "month" as its plotting variable.
# =============================================================================

s1_blood_pub <- s1_blood %>%

  filter(
    !is.na(value),
    value > 0,
    !is.na(group),
    !is.na(time_raw),
    !is.na(sheep_id)
  ) %>%

  mutate(

    month =
      suppressWarnings(
        readr::parse_number(
          as.character(time_raw)
        )
      )

  ) %>%

  filter(
    !is.na(month)
  )


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Study 1 mean ± SE
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

s1_blood_pub_summary <- s1_blood_pub %>%

  group_by(
    group,
    month
  ) %>%

  summarise(

    n_ewe =
      n_distinct(
        sheep_id
      ),

    n_obs =
      n(),

    mean_se =
      mean(
        value,
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),

    sd_se =
      sd(
        value,
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),

    se_se =
      sd_se /
      sqrt(
        n_obs
      ),

    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%

  arrange(
    group,
    month
  )


# =============================================================================
# 4. CREATE STUDY 2 WHOLE-BLOOD PUBLICATION DATA # =============================================================================
#
# Study 2 uses actual sampling dates in the statistical analysis.
# For the publication figure, observed sampling dates are converted # to sequential study-month positions.
# =============================================================================

study2_sample_dates <- sort(
  unique(
    s2_blood$sample_date[
      !is.na(
        s2_blood$sample_date
      )
    ]
  )
)


s2_blood_pub <- s2_blood %>%

  filter(
    !is.na(value),
    value > 0,
    !is.na(group),
    !is.na(sample_date),
    !is.na(sheep_id)
  ) %>%

  mutate(

    study_month =
      match(
        sample_date,
        study2_sample_dates
      )

  )


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Study 2 mean ± SE
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

s2_blood_pub_summary <- s2_blood_pub %>%

  group_by(
    group,
    study_month
  ) %>%

  summarise(

    n_ewe =
      n_distinct(
        sheep_id
      ),

    n_obs =
      n(),

    mean_se =
      mean(
        value,
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),

    sd_se =
      sd(
        value,
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),

    se_se =
      sd_se /
      sqrt(
        n_obs
      ),

    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%

  arrange(
    group,
    study_month
  )


# =============================================================================
# 5. QUICK QC
# =============================================================================

cat("\n============================================================\n")
cat("PUBLICATION FIGURE DATA QC\n")
cat("============================================================\n\n")

cat(
  "Study 1 Whole Blood observations:",
  nrow(s1_blood_pub),
  "\n"
)

cat(
  "Study 1 ewes:",
  n_distinct(s1_blood_pub$sheep_id),
  "\n\n"
)

cat(
  "Study 2 Whole Blood observations:",
  nrow(s2_blood_pub),
  "\n"
)

cat(
  "Study 2 ewes:",
  n_distinct(s2_blood_pub$sheep_id),
  "\n\n"
)


# =============================================================================
# 6. STUDY 1 WHOLE-BLOOD Se PANEL FUNCTION 
# =============================================================================

make_study1_blood_panel <- function(
  raw_data,
  summary_data,
  y_title,
  show_individuals = TRUE
) {

  p <- ggplot() +

    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Breeding period:
    # Cycle 1 = week 7
    # Cycle 2 = week 10
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------

    annotate(
      "rect",
      xmin = 7 / 4,
      xmax = 10 / 4,
      ymin = -Inf,
      ymax = Inf,
      fill = "grey60",
      alpha = 0.14
    ) +

    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # End of Se supplementation = week 12
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------

    geom_vline(
      xintercept = 12 / 4,
      linetype = "dashed",
      linewidth = 0.6,
      color = "grey20"
    )


  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Individual ewe trajectories
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

  if (show_individuals) {

    p <- p +

      geom_line(
        data = raw_data,
        aes(
          x = month,
          y = value,
          group = sheep_id,
          color = group
        ),
        linewidth = 0.38,
        alpha = 0.16
      ) +

      geom_point(
        data = raw_data,
        aes(
          x = month,
          y = value,
          color = group
        ),
        size = 0.8,
        alpha = 0.18
      )
  }


  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Treatment mean ± SE
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

  p +

    geom_errorbar(
      data = summary_data,
      aes(
        x = month,
        ymin = pmax(
          mean_se - se_se,
          0
        ),
        ymax = mean_se + se_se,
        color = group
      ),
      width = 0.12,
      linewidth = 0.55
    ) +

    geom_line(
      data = summary_data,
      aes(
        x = month,
        y = mean_se,
        color = group,
        linetype = group,
        group = group
      ),
      linewidth = 1.15
    ) +

    geom_point(
      data = summary_data,
      aes(
        x = month,
        y = mean_se,
        color = group,
        shape = group
      ),
      size = 2.7
    ) +

    scale_color_manual(
      values = treatment_colors,
      name = "Treatment"
    ) +

    scale_shape_manual(
      values = treatment_shapes,
      name = "Treatment"
    ) +

    scale_linetype_manual(
      values = treatment_linetypes,
      name = "Treatment"
    ) +

    scale_y_continuous(
      expand =
        expansion(
          mult = c(
            0.03,
            0.08
          )
        )
    ) +

    labs(
      title = NULL,
      x = "Study month",
      y = y_title
    ) +

    theme_publication()
}


# =============================================================================
# STUDY 2 — CONVERT IMPORTANT DATES TO FIGURE POSITIONS 
# =============================================================================

# Function to convert an actual date to its position on the # sequential Study 2 sampling-date x-axis date_to_study_month <- function(date_value) {


date_to_study_month <- function(date_value){
   if (is.na(date_value)) {
    return(NA_real_)
  }
  approx(
    x = as.numeric(study2_sample_dates),
    y = seq_along(study2_sample_dates),
    xout = as.numeric(date_value),
    rule = 2
  )$y
}


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Breeding period
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

study2_first_breeding_month <- date_to_study_month(
  study2_first_breeding_date
)

study2_last_breeding_month <- date_to_study_month(
  study2_last_breeding_date
)


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# End of selenium supplementation
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

study2_feed_stop_month <- date_to_study_month(
  STUDY2_FEED_STOP_DATE
)


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# QC — make sure all three positions were created # -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

cat("\n============================================================\n")
cat("STUDY 2 FIGURE DATE POSITIONS\n")
cat("============================================================\n")

cat(
  "First breeding date:",
  as.character(study2_first_breeding_date),
  " -> Study month:",
  round(study2_first_breeding_month, 2),
  "\n"
)

cat(

  " -> Study month:",

  "\n"
)

cat(

  as.character(STUDY2_FEED_STOP_DATE),
  " -> Study month:",
  round(study2_feed_stop_month, 2),
  "\n"
)



# =============================================================================
# 7. STUDY 2 WHOLE-BLOOD Se PANEL FUNCTION 
# =============================================================================

make_study2_blood_panel <- function(
  raw_data,
  summary_data,
  y_title,
  show_individuals = TRUE
) {

  p <- ggplot() +

    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Breeding period
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------

    annotate(
      "rect",
      xmin = study2_first_breeding_month,
      xmax = study2_last_breeding_month,
      ymin = -Inf,
      ymax = Inf,
      fill = "grey60",
      alpha = 0.14
    ) +

    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # End of Se supplementation
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------

    geom_vline(
      xintercept = study2_feed_stop_month,
      linetype = "dashed",
      linewidth = 0.6,
      color = "grey20"
    )


  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Individual ewe trajectories
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

  if (show_individuals) {

    p <- p +

      geom_line(
        data = raw_data,
        aes(
          x = study_month,
          y = value,
          group = sheep_id,
          color = group
        ),
        linewidth = 0.38,
        alpha = 0.16
      ) +

      geom_point(
        data = raw_data,
        aes(
          x = study_month,
          y = value,
          color = group
        ),
        size = 0.8,
        alpha = 0.18
      )
  }


  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Treatment mean ± SE
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

  p +

    geom_errorbar(
      data = summary_data,
      aes(
        x = study_month,
        ymin = pmax(
          mean_se - se_se,
          0
        ),
        ymax = mean_se + se_se,
        color = group
      ),
      width = 0.12,
      linewidth = 0.55
    ) +

    geom_line(
      data = summary_data,
      aes(
        x = study_month,
        y = mean_se,
        color = group,
        linetype = group,
        group = group
      ),
      linewidth = 1.15
    ) +

    geom_point(
      data = summary_data,
      aes(
        x = study_month,
        y = mean_se,
        color = group,
        shape = group
      ),
      size = 2.7
    ) +

    scale_color_manual(
      values = treatment_colors,
      name = "Treatment"
    ) +

    scale_shape_manual(
      values = treatment_shapes,
      name = "Treatment"
    ) +

    scale_linetype_manual(
      values = treatment_linetypes,
      name = "Treatment"
    ) +

    scale_x_continuous(
      breaks =
        seq_along(
          study2_sample_dates
        ),
      labels =
        seq_along(
          study2_sample_dates
        )
    ) +

    scale_y_continuous(
      expand =
        expansion(
          mult = c(
            0.03,
            0.08
          )
        )
    ) +

    labs(
      title = NULL,
      x = "Study month",
      y = y_title
    ) +

    theme_publication()
}
```
