### Stand alone plot for Study 2 Figure
```{r}

# =============================================================================
# STUDY 2 — STANDALONE WHOLE-BLOOD SELENIUM FIGURE # # Creates TWO publication versions:
#
#   1. Whole Blood Se (ppm)
#   2. Whole Blood Se (mg/kg)
#
# Figure includes:
#   - Individual ewe trajectories lightly plotted
#   - Individual ewe observations lightly plotted
#   - Treatment mean ± SE
#   - Grey shading = recorded breeding period
#   - Dashed vertical line = end of Se supplementation
#
# X-axis uses actual study weeks:
#
#   Study month 0 -> Week 0
#   Study month 2 -> Week 3
#   Study month 3 -> Week 6
#   Study month 4 -> Week 12
#   Study month 5 -> Week 15
#   Study month 6 -> Week 18
#   Study month 7 -> Week 24
#   Study month 8 -> Week 30
#
# Required objects from the main analysis:
#
#   s2_blood
#   study2_first_breeding_date
#   study2_last_breeding_date
#   STUDY2_FEED_STOP_DATE
#   PUB_FIG_DIR
#
# =============================================================================


library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(ragg)


# =============================================================================
# 1. COLOR-BLIND-SAFE TREATMENT PALETTE
# =============================================================================

treatment_colors <- c(
  "Control" = "#000000",
  "10 ppm"  = "#0072B2",
  "30 ppm"  = "#E69F00"
)


treatment_shapes <- c(
  "Control" = 16,
  "10 ppm"  = 17,
  "30 ppm"  = 15
)


treatment_linetypes <- c(
  "Control" = "solid",
  "10 ppm"  = "dashed",
  "30 ppm"  = "dotdash"
)


# =============================================================================
# 2. PUBLICATION THEME
# =============================================================================

theme_publication <- function() {

  theme_classic(
    base_size = 11,
    base_family = "Times New Roman"
  ) +

    theme(

      text =
        element_text(
          family = "Times New Roman",
          color = "black"
        ),

      axis.title =
        element_text(
          family = "Times New Roman",
          size = 11,
          face = "bold"
        ),

      axis.text =
        element_text(
          family = "Times New Roman",
          size = 10,
          color = "black"
        ),

      legend.title =
        element_text(
          family = "Times New Roman",
          size = 10,
          face = "bold"
        ),

      legend.text =
        element_text(
          family = "Times New Roman",
          size = 10
        ),

      legend.position = "top",

      panel.grid =
        element_blank(),

      plot.margin =
        margin(
          8,
          10,
          8,
          8
        )
    )
}


# =============================================================================
# 3. STUDY 2 SAMPLING-WEEK DEFINITIONS
# =============================================================================
#
# These are the eight actual Study 2 sampling occasions.
# =============================================================================

study2_weeks <- c(
  0,
  3,
  6,
  12,
  15,
  18,
  24,
  30
)


study2_months <- c(
  0,
  2,
  3,
  4,
  5,
  6,
  7,
  8
)


# =============================================================================
# 4. IDENTIFY ACTUAL STUDY 2 BLOOD-SAMPLING DATES # =============================================================================

study2_sample_dates <- sort(
  unique(
    s2_blood$sample_date[
      !is.na(
        s2_blood$sample_date
      )
    ]
  )
)


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Safety check
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

if (
  length(study2_sample_dates) != 8
) {

  stop(
    paste0(
      "Expected 8 Study 2 blood-sampling dates, but found ",
      length(study2_sample_dates),
      ". Check s2_blood$sample_date."
    )
  )
}


# =============================================================================
# 5. BUILD DATE -> MONTH -> WEEK LOOKUP TABLE # =============================================================================

study2_date_lookup <- data.frame(

  sample_date =
    study2_sample_dates,

  study_month =
    study2_months,

  study_week =
    study2_weeks

)


cat("\n")
cat("============================================================\n")
cat("STUDY 2 — SAMPLING DATE / MONTH / WEEK MAPPING\n")
cat("============================================================\n\n")


print(
  study2_date_lookup
)


# =============================================================================
# 6. CREATE RAW STUDY 2 PUBLICATION DATA # =============================================================================

s2_blood_pub <- s2_blood %>%

  filter(
    !is.na(value),
    value > 0,
    !is.na(group),
    !is.na(sample_date),
    !is.na(sheep_id)
  ) %>%

  left_join(
    study2_date_lookup,
    by = "sample_date"
  )


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Make sure every observation was assigned a week # -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

if (
  any(
    is.na(
      s2_blood_pub$study_week
    )
  )
) {

  stop(
    "At least one Study 2 blood observation could not be assigned to a study week."
  )
}


# =============================================================================
# 7. CALCULATE TREATMENT MEAN ± SE
# =============================================================================

s2_blood_pub_summary <- s2_blood_pub %>%

  group_by(
    group,
    study_month,
    study_week
  ) %>%

  summarise(

    n_ewe =
      n_distinct(
        sheep_id
      ),

    n_obs =
      n(),

    mean_se =
      mean(
        value,
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),

    sd_se =
      sd(
        value,
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),

    se_se =
      sd_se /
      sqrt(
        n_obs
      ),

    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%

  arrange(
    group,
    study_week
  )


# =============================================================================
# 8. CONVERT CALENDAR DATES TO STUDY-WEEK POSITIONS # =============================================================================
#
# The breeding dates and Se feed-stop date do not necessarily fall # exactly on blood-sampling dates.
#
# Therefore, their positions are interpolated between the known # sampling dates and their corresponding study weeks.
# =============================================================================

date_to_study_week <- function(target_date) {

  approx(

    x =
      as.numeric(
        study2_date_lookup$sample_date
      ),

    y =
      study2_date_lookup$study_week,

    xout =
      as.numeric(
        target_date
      ),

    rule = 2

  )$y
}


# =============================================================================
# 9. CALCULATE BREEDING AND FEED-STOP POSITIONS # =============================================================================

study2_first_breeding_week <- date_to_study_week(
  study2_first_breeding_date
)


study2_last_breeding_week <- date_to_study_week(
  study2_last_breeding_date
)


study2_feed_stop_week <- date_to_study_week(
  STUDY2_FEED_STOP_DATE
)


# =============================================================================
# 10. QC — IMPORTANT EVENT POSITIONS
# =============================================================================

cat("\n")
cat("============================================================\n")
cat("STUDY 2 — FIGURE EVENT POSITIONS\n")
cat("============================================================\n\n")


cat(
  "First breeding date: ",
  as.character(
    study2_first_breeding_date
  ),
  "\n",
  sep = ""
)


cat(
  "First breeding week: ",
  round(
    study2_first_breeding_week,
    2
  ),
  "\n\n",
  sep = ""
)


cat(
  "Last breeding date: ",
  as.character(
    study2_last_breeding_date
  ),
  "\n",
  sep = ""
)


cat(
  "Last breeding week: ",
  round(
    study2_last_breeding_week,
    2
  ),
  "\n\n",
  sep = ""
)


cat(
  "Se supplementation stopped: ",
  as.character(
    STUDY2_FEED_STOP_DATE
  ),
  "\n",
  sep = ""
)


cat(
  "Feed-stop week: ",
  round(
    study2_feed_stop_week,
    2
  ),
  "\n",
  sep = ""
)


# =============================================================================
# 11. DATA QC
# =============================================================================

cat("\n")
cat("============================================================\n")
cat("STUDY 2 — WHOLE-BLOOD Se DATA QC\n")
cat("============================================================\n\n")


cat(
  "Number of observations: ",
  nrow(
    s2_blood_pub
  ),
  "\n",
  sep = ""
)


cat(
  "Number of ewes: ",
  n_distinct(
    s2_blood_pub$sheep_id
  ),
  "\n",
  sep = ""
)


cat(
  "Number of sampling occasions: ",
  n_distinct(
    s2_blood_pub$study_week
  ),
  "\n\n",
  sep = ""
)


# =============================================================================
# 12. STUDY 2 WHOLE-BLOOD Se PLOTTING FUNCTION # =============================================================================

make_study2_blood_figure <- function(
  y_axis_title
) {

  ggplot() +

    # =========================================================================
    # SHADED BREEDING PERIOD
    # =========================================================================

    annotate(
      "rect",
      xmin = study2_first_breeding_week,
      xmax = study2_last_breeding_week,
      ymin = -Inf,
      ymax = Inf,
      fill = "grey60",
      alpha = 0.14
    ) +

    # =========================================================================
    # END OF Se SUPPLEMENTATION
    # =========================================================================

    geom_vline(
      xintercept = study2_feed_stop_week,
      linetype = "dashed",
      linewidth = 0.6,
      color = "grey20"
    ) +

    # =========================================================================
    # INDIVIDUAL EWE TRAJECTORIES
    # =========================================================================

    geom_line(
      data = s2_blood_pub,

      aes(
        x = study_week,
        y = value,
        group = sheep_id,
        color = group
      ),

      linewidth = 0.38,
      alpha = 0.16
    ) +

    # =========================================================================
    # INDIVIDUAL EWE OBSERVATIONS
    # =========================================================================

    geom_point(
      data = s2_blood_pub,

      aes(
        x = study_week,
        y = value,
        color = group
      ),

      size = 0.8,
      alpha = 0.18
    ) +

    # =========================================================================
    # TREATMENT MEAN ± SE
    # =========================================================================

    geom_errorbar(
      data = s2_blood_pub_summary,

      aes(
        x = study_week,

        ymin =
          pmax(
            mean_se - se_se,
            0
          ),

        ymax =
          mean_se + se_se,

        color = group
      ),

      width = 0.45,
      linewidth = 0.55
    ) +

    # =========================================================================
    # TREATMENT MEAN LINES
    # =========================================================================

    geom_line(
      data = s2_blood_pub_summary,

      aes(
        x = study_week,
        y = mean_se,
        color = group,
        linetype = group,
        group = group
      ),

      linewidth = 1.15
    ) +

    # =========================================================================
    # TREATMENT MEAN POINTS
    # =========================================================================

    geom_point(
      data = s2_blood_pub_summary,

      aes(
        x = study_week,
        y = mean_se,
        color = group,
        shape = group
      ),

      size = 2.8
    ) +

    # =========================================================================
    # TREATMENT COLORS / SHAPES / LINE TYPES
    # =========================================================================

    scale_color_manual(
      values = treatment_colors,
      name = "Treatment"
    ) +

    scale_shape_manual(
      values = treatment_shapes,
      name = "Treatment"
    ) +

    scale_linetype_manual(
      values = treatment_linetypes,
      name = "Treatment"
    ) +

    # =========================================================================
    # X AXIS — ACTUAL STUDY WEEKS
    # =========================================================================

    scale_x_continuous(

      breaks = c(
        0,
        3,
        6,
        12,
        15,
        18,
        24,
        30
      ),

      labels = c(
        "0",
        "3",
        "6",
        "12",
        "15",
        "18",
        "24",
        "30"
      ),

      limits = c(
        0,
        30
      ),

      expand =
        expansion(
          mult = c(
            0.01,
            0.02
          )
        )
    ) +

    # =========================================================================
    # Y AXIS
    # =========================================================================

    scale_y_continuous(

      expand =
        expansion(
          mult = c(
            0.03,
            0.08
          )
        )
    ) +

    # =========================================================================
    # AXIS LABELS
    #
    # No figure title
    # =========================================================================

    labs(
      title = NULL,
      x = "Week",
      y = y_axis_title
    ) +

    theme_publication()
}


# =============================================================================
# 13. VERSION 1 — ppm
# =============================================================================

figure_study2_ppm <- make_study2_blood_figure(

  y_axis_title =
    "Whole Blood Se (ppm)"

)


figure_study2_ppm


# =============================================================================
# 14. VERSION 2 — mg/kg
# =============================================================================

figure_study2_mgkg <- make_study2_blood_figure(

    "Whole Blood Se (mg/kg)"

)


figure_study2_mgkg


# =============================================================================
# 15. SAVE PDF — ppm
# =============================================================================

ggsave(
```

#### Weights for Study 1 & 2
```{r}
# ============================================================
# STARTING AND FINAL WEIGHT BY TREATMENT GROUP # Study 1 + Study 2 # ============================================================

library(dplyr)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# STUDY 1
# ------------------------------------------------------------

s1_start_final <- s1_weight %>%
  arrange(sheep_id, time_raw) %>%
  group_by(sheep_id) %>%
  summarise(
    group = first(group),
    starting_weight = first(value),
    final_weight = last(value),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

s1_weight_summary <- s1_start_final %>%
  group_by(group) %>%
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    starting_median = median(starting_weight, na.rm = TRUE),
    starting_sd = sd(starting_weight, na.rm = TRUE),
    final_median = median(final_weight, na.rm = TRUE),
    final_sd = sd(final_weight, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(study = "Study 1", .before = 1)


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# STUDY 2
# ------------------------------------------------------------

s2_start_final <- s2_weight %>%
  arrange(sheep_id, sample_date) %>%
  group_by(sheep_id) %>%
  summarise(
    group = first(group),
    starting_weight = first(value),
    final_weight = last(value),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

s2_weight_summary <- s2_start_final %>%
  group_by(group) %>%
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    starting_median = median(starting_weight, na.rm = TRUE),
    starting_sd = sd(starting_weight, na.rm = TRUE),
    final_median = median(final_weight, na.rm = TRUE),
    final_sd = sd(final_weight, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(study = "Study 2", .before = 1)


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# COMBINE + PRINT
# ------------------------------------------------------------

weight_summary <- bind_rows(
  s1_weight_summary,
  s2_weight_summary
)

print(weight_summary, n = Inf)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# OVERALL STARTING + FINAL WEIGHT 
# ENTIRE population within each study
# ------------------------------------------------------------

overall_weight_summary <- bind_rows(
  s1_start_final %>% mutate(study = "Study 1"),
  s2_start_final %>% mutate(study = "Study 2")
) %>% 
  group_by(study) %>%
  summarize(
    n = n(),
    starting_median = median(starting_weight, na.rm = TRUE),
    starting_sd = sd(starting_weight, na.rm = TRUE),
    final_median = median(final_weight, na.rm = TRUE),
    final_sd = sd(final_weight, na.rm = TRUE),
    ,groups = "drop"
  )
print(overall_weight_summary)

write.csv(
  overall_weight_summary,
  "Overall_Starting_Final_Weight_Summary.csv",
  row.names = FALSE
)

cat("\nSaved: Overall_Staring_Final_Weight_Summary.csv\n")

# find the median for the entire population.
# Create a table instead of figure 2. Model it like Table 1 from "Effect of Vitamin E Supplementation on Reproductive Performance in Spring Mate Ewes". Maybe add some statisitics into the table as well. 
# Jounral on animal science. 
# Small ruminant research.


# ============================================================
# OVERALL STARTING + FINAL WEIGHT
# Mean ± SD + Median/IQR
# ============================================================

overall_weight_summary <- bind_rows(
  s1_start_final %>% mutate(study = "Study 1"),
  s2_start_final %>% mutate(study = "Study 2")
) %>%
  group_by(study) %>%
  summarise(
    n = n(),

    starting_mean = mean(starting_weight, na.rm = TRUE),
    starting_sd = sd(starting_weight, na.rm = TRUE),
    starting_median = median(starting_weight, na.rm = TRUE),
    starting_iqr = IQR(starting_weight, na.rm = TRUE),

    final_mean = mean(final_weight, na.rm = TRUE),
    final_sd = sd(final_weight, na.rm = TRUE),
    final_median = median(final_weight, na.rm = TRUE),
    final_iqr = IQR(final_weight, na.rm = TRUE),

    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    starting_mean_sd = sprintf(
      "%.2f ± %.2f",
      starting_mean,
      starting_sd
    ),

    final_mean_sd = sprintf(
      "%.2f ± %.2f",
      final_mean,
      final_sd
    ),

    starting_median_iqr = sprintf(
      "%.2f [IQR %.2f]",
      starting_median,
      starting_iqr
    ),

    final_median_iqr = sprintf(
      "%.2f [IQR %.2f]",
      final_median,
      final_iqr
    )
  )

print(overall_weight_summary)

# Save CSV
write.csv(
  overall_weight_summary,
  "Overall_Starting_Final_Weight_Summary.csv",
  row.names = FALSE
)
```

### Table1
```{r}

# =============================================================================
# STUDY 2 — COMPLETE MANUSCRIPT TABLE
#
# Table structure:
#
#   Number of ewes
#
#   Body weight
#       Initial weight (Week 0)
#       Week 12 weight
#       Initial-to-Week-12 weight change
#
#   Breeding requirement (%)
#       One cycle
#       Repeated
#
#   Fertility (%)
#       Open
#       Lambed
#
#
# IMPORTANT:
#   Weight change is calculated WITHIN EWE:
#
#       Week 12 weight - Week 0 weight
#
#   The code also prints overall Study 2 population:
#
#       Week 0 weight       = mean ± SD
#       Week 12 weight      = mean ± SD
#       Week 0→12 change    = mean ± SD
#
#
# Required existing objects:
#
#   study2_repro
#   s2_weight
#
# =============================================================================


library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)


# =============================================================================
# 1. TREATMENT ORDER
# =============================================================================

study2_groups <- c(
  "Control",
  "10 ppm",
  "30 ppm"
)


# =============================================================================
# 2. NUMBER OF EWES PER TREATMENT
# =============================================================================

study2_n <- study2_repro %>%

  filter(
    !is.na(group),
    group %in% study2_groups
  ) %>%

  distinct(
    sheep_id,
    group
  ) %>%

  count(
    group,
    name = "n"
  ) %>%

  mutate(
    group = factor(
      group,
      levels = study2_groups
    )
  ) %>%

  arrange(
    group
  )


cat("\n")
cat("============================================================\n")
cat("STUDY 2 — NUMBER OF EWES\n")
cat("============================================================\n\n")

print(
  study2_n
)



# =============================================================================
# 3. CALCULATE ACTUAL STUDY WEEK FOR BODY-WEIGHT MEASUREMENTS # =============================================================================
#
# IMPORTANT:
# Weight has 10 sampling dates, so we DO NOT force the 8-date blood # sampling schedule onto the weight data.
#
# Instead:
#
#   Week 0 = first Study 2 weight measurement date
#
# and elapsed study week is calculated directly from the actual # calendar date.
# =============================================================================


study2_weight_start_date <- min(
  s2_weight$sample_date,
  na.rm = TRUE
)


s2_weight_table <- s2_weight %>%

  filter(
    !is.na(value),
    !is.na(sheep_id),
    !is.na(group),
    !is.na(sample_date),
    group %in% study2_groups
  ) %>%

  mutate(

    days_from_start =
      as.numeric(
        sample_date -
        study2_weight_start_date
      ),

    study_week =
      days_from_start / 7,

    group =
      factor(
        group,
        levels = study2_groups
      )
  )


# =============================================================================
# 4. QC — SHOW ALL 10 ACTUAL WEIGHT SAMPLING DATES # =============================================================================

study2_weight_date_qc <- s2_weight_table %>%

  distinct(
    sample_date,
    days_from_start,
    study_week
  ) %>%

  arrange(
    sample_date
  )


cat("\n")
cat("============================================================\n")
cat("STUDY 2 — ACTUAL WEIGHT SAMPLING DATES\n")
cat("============================================================\n\n")


print(
  study2_weight_date_qc,
  n = Inf
)


# =============================================================================
# 5. IDENTIFY WEEK 0 AND THE WEIGHT DATE CLOSEST TO WEEK 12 # =============================================================================
#
# Week 0:
#   first weight sampling date
#
# Week 12:
#   actual weight sampling date closest to 84 days after Week 0
#
# This avoids assuming that a measurement occurred on exactly Day 84.
# =============================================================================


week0_date <-
  study2_weight_start_date


target_week12_date <-
  study2_weight_start_date +
  84


week12_date <- study2_weight_date_qc %>%

  mutate(

    distance_from_week12 =
      abs(
        as.numeric(
          sample_date -
          target_week12_date
        )
      )
  ) %>%

  arrange(
    distance_from_week12
  ) %>%

  slice(
    1
  ) %>%

  pull(
    sample_date
  )


actual_week12 <- as.numeric(
  week12_date -
  week0_date
) / 7


cat("\n")
cat("============================================================\n")
cat("STUDY 2 — SELECTED WEIGHT DATES\n")
cat("============================================================\n\n")


cat(
  "Week 0 date: ",
  as.character(
    week0_date
  ),
  "\n",
  sep = ""
)


cat(
  "Target Week 12 date: ",
  as.character(
    target_week12_date
  ),
  "\n",
  sep = ""
)


cat(
  "Selected Week 12 date: ",
  as.character(
    week12_date
  ),
  "\n",
  sep = ""
)


cat(
  "Selected date corresponds to study week: ",
  round(
    actual_week12,
    2
  ),
  "\n",
  sep = ""
)


# =============================================================================
# 6. EXTRACT WEEK 0 AND WEEK 12 WEIGHTS
# =============================================================================
#
# Only the two selected sampling dates are used here.
# =============================================================================


study2_weight_0_12 <- s2_weight_table %>%

  filter(
    sample_date %in% c(
      week0_date,
      week12_date
    )
  ) %>%

  mutate(

    weight_time =
      case_when(

        sample_date == week0_date ~
          "week0_weight",

        sample_date == week12_date ~
          "week12_weight",

        TRUE ~
          NA_character_
      )
  ) %>%

  group_by(
    sheep_id,
    group,
    weight_time
  ) %>%

  summarise(

    weight =
      mean(
        value,
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),

    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%

  select(
    sheep_id,
    group,
    weight_time,
    weight
  ) %>%

  pivot_wider(

    names_from =
      weight_time,

    values_from =
      weight
  ) %>%

  mutate(

    weight_change_0_12 =
      week12_weight -
      week0_weight
  )


cat("\n")
cat("============================================================\n")
cat("STUDY 2 — INDIVIDUAL WEEK 0 AND WEEK 12 WEIGHTS\n")
cat("============================================================\n\n")


print(
  study2_weight_0_12,
  n = Inf
)

        !is.na(
          week0_weight
        )
      ),

    week12_available =
      sum(
        !is.na(
          week12_weight
        )
      ),

    complete_pairs =
      sum(
        !is.na(
          week0_weight
        ) &
        !is.na(
          week12_weight
        )
      )
  )


cat("\n")
cat("============================================================\n")
cat("STUDY 2 — WEEK 0 / WEEK 12 COMPLETENESS\n")
cat("============================================================\n\n")


print(

# =============================================================================
# 11. BODY-WEIGHT P-VALUES
# =============================================================================
#
# Three separate treatment comparisons:
#
#   1. Week 0 weight
#   2. Week 12 weight
#   3. Week 0 → Week 12 change
#
# =============================================================================


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Week 0
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

study2_week0_model <- lm(

  week0_weight ~ group,

  data =
    study2_weight_0_12
)


study2_week0_anova <- anova(
  study2_week0_model
)


study2_week0_p <-
  study2_week0_anova$`Pr(>F)`[1]


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Week 12
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

study2_week12_model <- lm(

  week12_weight ~ group,

  data =
    study2_weight_0_12
)


study2_week12_anova <- anova(
  study2_week12_model
)


study2_week12_p <-
  study2_week12_anova$`Pr(>F)`[1]


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Week 0 → Week 12 change
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

study2_weight_change_model <- lm(

  weight_change_0_12 ~ group,

  data =
    study2_weight_0_12
)


study2_weight_change_anova <- anova(
  study2_weight_change_model
)


study2_weight_change_p <-
  study2_weight_change_anova$`Pr(>F)`[1]


cat("\n")
cat("============================================================\n")
cat("STUDY 2 — BODY-WEIGHT P-VALUES\n")
cat("============================================================\n\n")

)


cat(

  ),

)


cat(
  "Week 0 to Week 12 change: P = ",

    digits = 4,

  ),
  "\n",
  sep = ""
)

study2_breeding_table_data <- study2_repro %>%

  filter(
    !is.na(group),
    group %in% study2_groups,
    !is.na(n_breeding_cycles)
  ) %>%

  mutate(

    breeding_status =
      if_else(
        n_breeding_cycles > 1,
        "Repeated",
        "One cycle"
      ),

    breeding_status =
      factor(
        breeding_status,
        levels = c(
          "One cycle",
          "Repeated"
        )
      ),

    group =
      factor(
        group,
        levels = study2_groups
      )
  )


# =============================================================================
# 13. BREEDING REQUIREMENT — n (%)
# =============================================================================

study2_breeding_summary <- study2_breeding_table_data %>%

  count(
    group,
    breeding_status,
    name = "n"
  ) %>%

  complete(

    group =
      factor(
        study2_groups,
        levels = study2_groups
      ),

    breeding_status =
      factor(
        c(
          "One cycle",
          "Repeated"
        ),
        levels = c(
          "One cycle",
          "Repeated"
        )
      ),

    fill =
      list(
        n = 0
      )
  ) %>%

  group_by(
    group
  ) %>%

  mutate(

    total =
      sum(n),

    percent =
      100 *
      n /
      total,

    display =
      sprintf(
        "%d (%.1f%%)",
        n,
        percent
      )
  ) %>%

  ungroup()


# =============================================================================
# 14. BREEDING REQUIREMENT — GLOBAL FISHER TEST # =============================================================================

study2_breeding_contingency <- table(

  study2_breeding_table_data$group,

  study2_breeding_table_data$breeding_status
)


set.seed(42)


study2_breeding_fisher <- fisher.test(

  study2_breeding_contingency,

  simulate.p.value = TRUE,

  B = 100000
)


study2_breeding_p <-
  study2_breeding_fisher$p.value


cat("\n")
cat("============================================================\n")
cat("STUDY 2 — BREEDING REQUIREMENT\n")
cat("============================================================\n\n")


print(
  study2_breeding_contingency
)

  "\nBreeding requirement P = ",
  format.pval(
    study2_breeding_p,
    digits = 4,
    eps = 0.0001
  ),
  "\n",
  sep = ""
)

study2_fertility_data <- study2_repro %>%

  filter(

          "Lambed",

        ever_pregnant == 0 ~
          "Open",

        TRUE ~
          NA_character_
      ),

    fertility_status =
      factor(
        fertility_status,
        levels = c(
          "Open",
          "Lambed"
        )
      ),

    group =
      factor(
        group,
        levels = study2_groups
      )

        study2_groups,
        levels = study2_groups
      ),

    fertility_status =
      factor(
        c(
          "Open",

        ),
        levels = c(
          "Open",

        )
      ),

    fill =

      )

  ) %>%

      n /

      sprintf(
        "%d (%.1f%%)",
        n,
        percent
      )

# =============================================================================
# 17. FERTILITY — GLOBAL FISHER TEST
# =============================================================================

study2_fertility_contingency <- table(

)


set.seed(42)


study2_fertility_fisher <- fisher.test(

)

  study2_fertility_fisher$p.value


cat("\n")
cat("============================================================\n")
cat("STUDY 2 — FERTILITY\n")
cat("============================================================\n\n")


print(
  study2_fertility_contingency
)

# =============================================================================
# 18. P-VALUE FORMATTER
# =============================================================================

format_table_p <- function(p) {

  if (
    is.na(p)
  ) {

    return("")

  }


  if (
    p < 0.001
  ) {

    return("<0.001")

  }


  sprintf(
    "%.4f",
    p
  )
}

    row[[mean_variable]],
    row[[sd_variable]]

}
```

### Liver Se Concentration Analysis Given different time points
```{r}

# =============================================================================
# STUDY 1 — LIVER SELENIUM
# PAIRWISE TREATMENT COMPARISONS AT EACH SAMPLING TIME # # Existing model:
#
#   log(Se) ~ treatment * sampling_time + (1 | ewe)
#
# Questions answered:
#
#   At each sampling time:
#
#       Control vs 10 ppm
#       Control vs 30 ppm
#       Control vs 60 ppm
#       10 ppm vs 30 ppm
#       10 ppm vs 60 ppm
#       30 ppm vs 60 ppm
#
# Multiple comparisons:
#       Tukey adjustment
#
# =============================================================================


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. PACKAGES
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

library(dplyr)
library(emmeans)


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. GET EXISTING STUDY 1 LIVER MODEL
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
#
# study1_liver_model was created by the previous analysis.
#
# It contains:
#
#   $model
#   $anova
#   $data
#
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

liver_model <- study1_liver_model$model


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. CHECK MODEL
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

cat("\n")
cat("============================================================\n")
cat("STUDY 1 — LIVER SE MODEL\n")
cat("============================================================\n\n")

print(
  summary(
    liver_model
  )
)


cat("\n")
cat("============================================================\n")
cat("STUDY 1 — OVERALL FIXED EFFECTS\n")
cat("============================================================\n\n")

print(
  study1_liver_model$anova
)


# =============================================================================
# 4. ESTIMATED MARGINAL MEANS
# =============================================================================
#
# Calculate treatment means separately at EVERY sampling occasion.
#
# Because the model was fitted using log(Se), these estimates initially # exist on the log scale.
# =============================================================================

liver_emm <- emmeans(

  liver_model,

  ~ group | time_factor
)


cat("\n")
cat("============================================================\n")
cat("ESTIMATED MARGINAL MEANS — LOG SCALE\n")
cat("============================================================\n\n")

print(
  liver_emm
)


# =============================================================================
# 5. ALL PAIRWISE TREATMENT COMPARISONS WITHIN EACH TIME # =============================================================================
#
# This is the main analysis we want.
#
# For every sampling occasion, it compares:
#
#   Control - 10 ppm
#   Control - 30 ppm
#   Control - 60 ppm
#   10 ppm - 30 ppm
#   10 ppm - 60 ppm
#   30 ppm - 60 ppm
#
# Tukey adjustment controls for the multiple treatment comparisons # performed within each sampling occasion.
# =============================================================================

liver_pairwise <- pairs(

  liver_emm,

  adjust = "tukey"
)


cat("\n")
cat("============================================================\n")
cat("PAIRWISE LIVER SE COMPARISONS AT EACH TIME\n") 
cat("TUKEY-ADJUSTED P-VALUES\n")
cat("============================================================\n\n")

print(
  liver_pairwise
)


# =============================================================================
# 6. CONVERT RESULTS TO DATA FRAME
# =============================================================================

liver_pairwise_df <- as.data.frame(
  liver_pairwise
)


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Clean P-value formatting
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

liver_pairwise_df <- liver_pairwise_df %>%

  mutate(

    significance =
      case_when(

        p.value < 0.001 ~ "***",

        p.value < 0.01 ~ "**",

        p.value < 0.05 ~ "*",

        TRUE ~ "NS"
      ),

    p_formatted =
      case_when(

        p.value < 0.0001 ~
          "<0.0001",

        TRUE ~
          sprintf(
            "%.4f",
            p.value
          )
      )
  )


cat("\n")
cat("============================================================\n")
cat("ALL PAIRWISE RESULTS\n")
cat("============================================================\n\n")

print(
  liver_pairwise_df
)


# =============================================================================
# 7. SHOW ONLY STATISTICALLY SIGNIFICANT COMPARISONS # =============================================================================

liver_significant <- liver_pairwise_df %>%

  filter(
    p.value < 0.05
  ) %>%

  arrange(
    time_factor,
    p.value
  )


cat("\n")
cat("============================================================\n")
cat("SIGNIFICANT LIVER SE TREATMENT COMPARISONS\n") 
cat("P < 0.05 AFTER TUKEY ADJUSTMENT\n")
cat("============================================================\n\n")

print(
  liver_significant
)


# =============================================================================
# 8. SPECIFICALLY LOOK AT 60-PPM COMPARISONS # =============================================================================
#
# This pulls every comparison involving 60 ppm.
#
# =============================================================================

liver_60ppm <- liver_pairwise_df %>%

  filter(
    grepl(
      "60 ppm",
      contrast,
      fixed = TRUE
    )
  ) %>%

  arrange(
    time_factor
  )


cat("\n")
cat("============================================================\n")
cat("60-PPM LIVER SE COMPARISONS\n")
cat("============================================================\n\n")

print(
  liver_60ppm
)


# =============================================================================
# 9. SPECIFICALLY: 60 PPM VS 10 PPM
# =============================================================================

liver_60_vs_10 <- liver_pairwise_df %>%

  filter(

    grepl(
      "60 ppm",
      contrast,
      fixed = TRUE
    ),

    grepl(
      "10 ppm",
      contrast,
      fixed = TRUE
    )
  ) %>%

  arrange(
    time_factor
  )


cat("\n")
cat("============================================================\n")
cat("60 PPM VS 10 PPM — BY SAMPLING TIME\n")
cat("============================================================\n\n")

print(
  liver_60_vs_10
)


# =============================================================================
# 10. BACK-TRANSFORM ESTIMATED MEANS
# =============================================================================
#
# Because:
#
#       log_se = log(value)
#
# exponentiating the estimated means returns geometric means on the # original Se concentration scale.
#
# =============================================================================

liver_emm_original <- summary(

  liver_emm,

  type = "response"
)


cat("\n")
cat("============================================================\n")
cat("LIVER SE ESTIMATED MEANS — ORIGINAL SCALE\n")
cat("============================================================\n\n")

print(
  liver_emm_original
)


# =============================================================================
# 11. PAIRWISE RATIOS ON ORIGINAL SE SCALE # =============================================================================
#
# This is particularly useful biologically.
#
# For example:
#
#       ratio = 3
#
# means one treatment has approximately 3x the liver Se concentration # of the other treatment at that sampling occasion.
#
# =============================================================================

liver_pairwise_ratio <- summary(

  pairs(
    liver_emm,
    adjust = "tukey"
  ),

  type = "response",

  infer = c(
    TRUE,
    TRUE
  )
)


liver_pairwise_ratio_df <- as.data.frame(
  liver_pairwise_ratio
)


cat("\n")
cat("============================================================\n")
cat("LIVER SE TREATMENT RATIOS — ORIGINAL SCALE\n")
cat("============================================================\n\n")

print(
  liver_pairwise_ratio_df
)


# =============================================================================
# 12. 60 PPM COMPARISONS — ORIGINAL SCALE # =============================================================================

liver_60ppm_ratio <- liver_pairwise_ratio_df %>%

  filter(
    grepl(
      "60 ppm",
      contrast,
      fixed = TRUE
    )
  )


cat("\n")
cat("============================================================\n")
cat("60-PPM COMPARISONS — ORIGINAL SE SCALE\n")
cat("============================================================\n\n")

print(
  liver_60ppm_ratio
)


# =============================================================================
# 13. RAW LIVER SE DESCRIPTIVE STATISTICS # =============================================================================
#
# These are NOT the model-adjusted estimates.
#
# They are useful for understanding the actual observed concentrations # behind the model results.
# =============================================================================

liver_raw_summary <- study1_liver_model$data %>%

  group_by(
    time_factor,
    group
  ) %>%

  summarise(

    n =
      sum(
        !is.na(value)
      ),

    mean_se =
      mean(
        value,
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),

    sd_se =
      sd(
        value,
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),

    median_se =
      median(
        value,
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),

    min_se =
      min(
        value,
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),

    max_se =
      max(
        value,
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),

    .groups = "drop"
  )


cat("\n")
cat("============================================================\n")
cat("RAW LIVER SE CONCENTRATIONS BY TREATMENT AND TIME\n")
cat("============================================================\n\n")

print(
  liver_raw_summary
)


# =============================================================================
# 14. FINAL COMPACT RESULTS TABLE
# =============================================================================
#
# Useful table for us to review together.
# =============================================================================

liver_results_table <- liver_pairwise_ratio_df %>%

  mutate(

    significance =
      case_when(

        p.value < 0.001 ~ "***",

        p.value < 0.01 ~ "**",

        p.value < 0.05 ~ "*",

        TRUE ~ "NS"
      ),

    p_formatted =
      case_when(

        p.value < 0.0001 ~
          "<0.0001",

        TRUE ~
          sprintf(
            "%.4f",
            p.value
          )
      )
  ) %>%

  arrange(
    time_factor,
    p.value
  )


cat("\n")
cat("============================================================\n")
cat("FINAL LIVER SE PAIRWISE COMPARISON TABLE\n")
cat("============================================================\n\n")

print(
  liver_results_table
)


```


### Final weight comparison of initial start time
```{r}

# =============================================================================
# STUDY 2 — OVERALL INITIAL BODY WEIGHT
#
# Purpose:
#   Calculate the initial body weight for the TOTAL Study 2 population.
#
#   No treatment-group stratification.
#
# Output:
#   N
#   Mean initial weight
#   SD
#   Mean ± SD
#   Median
#   Min
#   Max
# =============================================================================


library(dplyr)


# =============================================================================
# 1. CHECK THE WEIGHT DATA
# =============================================================================

cat("\n")
cat("============================================================\n")
cat("STUDY 2 WEIGHT DATA\n")
cat("============================================================\n\n")

print(
  s2_weight %>%
    arrange(
      sheep_id,
      sample_date
    )
)


# =============================================================================
# 2. IDENTIFY EACH EWE'S INITIAL WEIGHT
# =============================================================================
#
# For each ewe:
#   - arrange measurements chronologically
#   - retain the earliest available non-missing body weight
#
# This ensures that each ewe contributes ONE initial weight.
# =============================================================================

study2_initial_weight <- s2_weight %>%

  filter(
    !is.na(value),
    !is.na(sample_date)
  ) %>%

  arrange(
    sheep_id,
    sample_date
  ) %>%

  group_by(
    sheep_id
  ) %>%

  slice_head(
    n = 1
  ) %>%

  ungroup()


# =============================================================================
# 3. QC — SHOW INITIAL WEIGHT FOR EACH EWE # =============================================================================

cat("\n")
cat("============================================================\n")
cat("INITIAL BODY WEIGHT FOR EACH EWE\n")
cat("============================================================\n\n")

print(
  study2_initial_weight %>%
    select(
      sheep_id,
      group,
      sample_date,
      value
    )
)


# =============================================================================
# 4. CALCULATE TOTAL-POPULATION INITIAL BODY WEIGHT # =============================================================================
#
# IMPORTANT:
#   There is NO group_by(group) here.
#
# Therefore, these statistics describe the entire Study 2 population.
# =============================================================================

study2_initial_weight_overall <- study2_initial_weight %>%

  summarise(

    n = n(),

    mean_initial_weight =
      mean(
        value,
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),

    sd_initial_weight =
      sd(
        value,
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),

    median_initial_weight =
      median(
        value,
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),

    min_initial_weight =
      min(
        value,
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),

    max_initial_weight =
      max(
        value,
        na.rm = TRUE
      )
  )


# =============================================================================
# 5. PRINT NUMERICAL RESULTS
# =============================================================================

cat("\n")
cat("============================================================\n")
cat("STUDY 2 — OVERALL INITIAL BODY WEIGHT\n")
cat("============================================================\n\n")

print(
  study2_initial_weight_overall
)


# =============================================================================
# 6. PRINT AS MEAN ± SD
# =============================================================================

mean_weight <- study2_initial_weight_overall$mean_initial_weight

sd_weight <- study2_initial_weight_overall$sd_initial_weight

n_weight <- study2_initial_weight_overall$n


cat("\n")
cat("============================================================\n")
cat("MANUSCRIPT FORMAT\n")
cat("============================================================\n\n")

cat(
  sprintf(
    "Overall initial body weight: %.2f ± %.2f (n = %d)\n",
    mean_weight,
    sd_weight,
    n_weight
  )
)


# =============================================================================
# 7. OPTIONAL — JUST THE VALUE FOR COPYING INTO THE MANUSCRIPT # =============================================================================

cat("\n")

cat(
  sprintf(
    "%.2f ± %.2f",
    mean_weight,
    sd_weight
  )
)

cat("\n")


```
